ecosystem.title: One order, end to end
ecosystem.lede: Read it like a paper roll: time runs left to right, from setting up the network to a delivered parcel and what can go wrong after it.

phases.title: Set up the network
phases.plain: Before anything can be sold, the network needs places, products and partners: nodes and lanes, buildings with shelves, a product master, vendors and sellers.

phases.title: Bring supply in
phases.plain: Stock is announced, a dock door is booked, the truck arrives at the gate, and dock staff count what is on it until the receipt is closed.

phases.title: Store it and keep it pickable
phases.plain: Received units are stowed on a shelf, the slotting plan decides what belongs near the pick faces, and replenishment keeps those faces full.

phases.title: Offer it to shoppers
phases.plain: What the network can sell is listed with content and a price, and its availability follows the stock that is really there.

phases.title: Shop, promise and pay
phases.plain: A shopper fills a cart, sees delivery offers backed by a promise, checks out and pays. The phase ends when the order is placed.

phases.title: Source the order and hand it to a warehouse
phases.plain: The network decides which node serves each order line, then hands it over. The warehouse receives it, allocates stock to it and releases it.

phases.title: Plan and release the work
phases.plain: Capacity, shifts and process paths decide how much work the building can take. Work is then released to the floor, never in waves, but as capacity allows.

phases.title: Pick, pack and ship
phases.plain: Tasks appear, associates claim them, units are picked and packed, a load is built and closed, and the shipment leaves the dock.

phases.title: Move the parcel and deliver
phases.plain: A label is issued, the load travels between nodes on a scheduled departure, a last-mile wave takes it out for delivery, and the promise is kept or broken.

phases.title: When things go wrong, and after the sale
phases.plain: Exceptions are opened, triaged and resolved. A return is authorized, inspected and given a disposition, and the shopper is refunded.

checkout.oneLine: Turns a ready cart into a placed order: a binding price, an authorized payment and an order handed on, with recovery when a step gives no clear answer.

rows.title: Open a checkout session
rows.story: The shopper starts checkout from a ready cart. Checkout checks that every chosen delivery offer is still valid, gets a binding price quote from pricing and opens a session that lasts as long as the quote.

rows.title: Confirm and place the order
rows.story: The shopper confirms with a payment method token. Checkout has the exact quote total authorized, then places the order. Once the order is accepted the session is complete.

then.does: closes the shopper's cart as checked out
binds the order to the payment authorization and applies facts that waited for it

rows.title: Payment is declined
rows.story: The payment is refused, or the amount authorized is not the quote total, in which case the hold is released. The session is declined and the shopper may try another payment method until the quote runs out.

rows.title: The order needs new delivery offers
rows.story: When the order is placed, an offer turns out to have changed and the order service sends new ones. The session ends as requote required with those offers and the payment hold is released.

rows.title: The order is refused
rows.story: The order service rejects the order outright. The session fails with a code, an alert is raised and the payment hold is released.

rows.title: The order service does not answer
rows.story: The order service gives no clear answer. The session stays locked in placing and the shopper is told the order is still being processed. This is announced once, on the first unclear answer.

rows.title: Settle an order that was in doubt
rows.story: A sweep replays the stored order request with the same key until the order service answers. It alerts at 20 hours, and at 22 hours gives up, fails the session and releases the payment hold.
rows.policy: Every sweep, replay each unsettled order request and record the answer

then.does: closes the shopper's cart as checked out
binds the order to the payment authorization and applies facts that waited for it

rows.title: Settle a payment that never answered
rows.story: A session left authorizing for over 2 minutes asks customer-payments again with the same key to learn the true outcome. The purchase then carries on as after a normal confirmation.
rows.policy: Every sweep, any session authorizing for over 2 minutes asks again, with the same key

then.does: closes the shopper's cart as checked out
binds the order to the payment authorization and applies facts that waited for it

rows.title: Release a payment hold that is still owed
rows.story: When an order is refused or needs a requote, releasing the payment hold is recorded as a debt on the session. A sweep retries every minute until it works.
rows.policy: Every minute, retry each payment-hold release that is still owed

rows.title: Let a session expire with its quote
rows.story: A sweep expires every open or declined session whose price quote has run out. A session that is authorizing or placing is not touched.
rows.policy: Every sweep, an open or declined session past its quote expiry becomes expired

rows.title: Forget old order requests
rows.story: The stored order request is dropped 24 hours after a session closes. The session itself stays, and nothing is announced.
rows.policy: Every sweep, drop the stored order request of sessions closed over 24 hours ago

hotspots.text: How the cart takes the requoted offers is open. Checkout only carries them; whether anything writes them into the cart is not verified here.
If the order service never answers, the session stays locked for up to 22 hours before it fails and the payment hold is released.
Offers are checked only when the session opens. One that expires before confirmation surfaces later as a requote from the order service.
A failed release of a payment hold stays on the session as a debt, retried every minute. After an amount mismatch the shopper cannot confirm again until it clears.

customer-ordering.oneLine: Takes a shopper's order at checkout with a confirmed delivery promise for every shipment group, and follows each group until it is delivered, lost, returned or cancelled.

rows.title: Register a shopper
rows.story: A shopper is registered with an e-mail, which can be used only once, and may start with saved delivery addresses. This is a test shopper, with no real account behind it.

rows.title: Save a delivery address
rows.story: A shopper saves an address to reuse at checkout, up to twenty. At checkout the address is copied into the order, so later edits never change a placed order.

rows.title: Place an order
rows.story: Checkout makes and confirms a delivery promise for each shipment group, and only then stores the order. If an offer is stale, nothing is placed and fresh offers come back. Nothing is placed if delivery-promise is down.

then.does: queues one assignment for each shipment group
confirms any promise still provisional

rows.title: Release holds a failed checkout left behind
rows.story: If a later group fails to confirm, the promises already confirmed are cancelled. A cancel that itself fails is queued and retried until delivery-promise lets the capacity go.
rows.policy: Every pass, retry the promise cancels a failed checkout could not perform

then.does: cancels the confirmed promise and returns its capacity

rows.title: Ask to cancel an order
rows.story: The shopper asks to cancel every group not yet locked. It is a request: the group waits until order-sourcing answers, and a vendor that ships first wins.

then.does: cancels each group not yet locked, or refuses it
cancels the promises of the cancelled groups

rows.title: Cancel a group whose promise cannot be kept
rows.story: When delivery-promise finds no route that can still deliver, the group is cancelled at once rather than left open.
rows.policy: Whenever a promise is unkeepable, cancel its shipment group

then.does: cancels the group's assignment, or refuses it if already locked
cancels the group's promise

rows.title: Accept a cancellation
rows.story: order-sourcing confirms it cancelled the group. The group, and the order if nothing else remains, becomes Cancelled.
rows.policy: Whenever order-sourcing cancels a group, mark the group cancelled

rows.title: Accept a refusal to cancel
rows.story: If the group was already locked, order-sourcing refuses. The group goes back to Locked and the vendor ships.
rows.policy: Whenever order-sourcing refuses a cancel, put the group back to locked

rows.title: Follow a revised promise
rows.story: When delivery-promise moves a promise to a later window, the group's delivery window, ship-by and node move with it. A revision no newer than the stored one changes nothing.
rows.policy: Whenever a promise is revised, move the group's window to the new one

rows.title: Record the promise verdict
rows.story: The tracking view shows whether the promise was kept or broken, and by how many minutes. An at-risk promise shows its reason the same way.
rows.policy: Whenever a promise is kept or broken, record the verdict on the group

rows.title: Mark a group in fulfilment
rows.story: order-sourcing locks the group to a node. The group moves from Promised to Locked and the assignment is linked to it.
rows.policy: Whenever a group is locked at a node, mark it in fulfilment

rows.title: Mark a group shipped
rows.story: order-sourcing reports the packages. The group becomes Shipped, and deliveries that arrived early are replayed so the group can close at once.
rows.policy: Whenever a group ships, mark it shipped and replay early deliveries

rows.title: Close a group on delivery
rows.story: A package is delivered. A group is Delivered once every package it announced is delivered. A package shared by merged groups closes all of them.
rows.policy: Whenever a package is delivered, mark it for every group that names it

rows.title: Mark a group lost or returned
rows.story: One lost package loses the group, and one returned package returns it. Both are final.
rows.policy: Whenever a package is lost or returned, mark its group lost or returned

rows.title: Show the delivery window of the day
rows.story: The carrier narrows a package to a time window on the day. It shows on the tracking view only; the promise and the order are untouched. A delivery point flagged as failing twice shows as a notice the same way.
rows.policy: Whenever a package gets a day-of window, show it unless a newer one is stored

hotspots.text: If delivery-promise is slow or down, checkout answers 503. There is no fallback promise, so the shopper must retry.
The cancel check is advisory. A lock this context has not yet consumed is invisible, so order-sourcing's answer decides.
A delivery can arrive before the shipment it belongs to. It is stored and replayed later; an unknown order is skipped, not retried.
A shopper whose consolidated offer expired is re-quoted without that tier. This is an accepted limitation.
The ship-to route is called restricted, but the fleet has no authentication and none is planned here.

opportunities.text: Storefront callers must accept the fifth (consolidated) tier before any shopper can be offered it.
The MCP tools and agent skills could later show the window's time zone, as the REST API does.

customer-payments.oneLine: Holds the shopper's money: authorizes the total at checkout, captures it as groups ship, releases it on cancellation and refunds lost or returned packages.

rows.title: Authorize a payment
rows.story: Checkout asks for the quote total to be held on the shopper's payment method, split by shipment group. The payment provider's answer decides: held or declined. A session that already has a live hold gets it back unchanged.

rows.title: Cancel a hold that was never captured
rows.story: Checkout cancels a hold before anything has been captured. The payment provider voids it and every amount still waiting is released.

rows.title: Tie the hold to the order
rows.story: checkout reports that the order was placed. The order is attached to the hold, and any shipping or tracking news that arrived before the order was known is now applied.
rows.policy: Whenever a checkout completes, bind its order to the hold and apply the facts that waited

rows.title: Take the money when a group ships
rows.story: order-sourcing says a shipment group has shipped. Its share of the hold is captured at the payment provider and the tracking numbers are kept. If the order is not tied yet, the news waits.
rows.policy: Whenever a group ships, capture its share of the hold

rows.title: Release the money of a cancelled group
rows.story: order-sourcing says a group was cancelled. Its share of the hold is released and the hold at the payment provider shrinks, or is voided when nothing is left.
rows.policy: Whenever a group is cancelled, release its share of the hold

rows.title: Release the money of a group nobody can fill
rows.story: order-sourcing says no source can fulfil a group. It is handled like a cancellation: its share of the hold is released.
rows.policy: Whenever a group cannot be sourced, release its share of the hold

rows.title: Refund a lost package
rows.story: shipping-and-tracking says a package was lost. What was captured for the group that carried it goes back to the shopper, less anything already refunded.
rows.policy: Whenever a package is lost, refund what was captured for its group

rows.title: Refund a returned package
rows.story: shipping-and-tracking says a package came back to the sender. What was captured for its group is refunded, less anything already refunded.
rows.policy: Whenever a package is returned, refund what was captured for its group

rows.title: Refund by hand
rows.story: Operations request a refund for an order or one of its groups. It can never exceed what was captured. The payment provider is asked once; if it is unreachable the refund waits.

rows.title: Try a failed refund again
rows.story: Operations send a failed refund back to the payment provider. A refund gets at most five attempts in all.

rows.title: Finish refunds left waiting
rows.story: A sweep picks up refunds that sat requested for 30 seconds because the payment provider could not be reached, and asks the provider again.
rows.policy: Every sweep, any refund requested for over 30 seconds is sent to the provider again

rows.title: Renew a hold before it lapses
rows.story: A sweep asks the payment provider for a fresh hold 24 hours before the old one ends. If the provider declines, or the hold already lapsed, the authorization expires and what was still waiting is released.
rows.policy: Every sweep, a hold within 24 hours of its end is renewed or, failing that, expired

rows.title: Void holds nobody claimed
rows.story: A hold that no completed checkout tied to an order within 24 hours is voided. It is the safety net behind checkout's own give-up.
rows.policy: Every sweep, a hold with no order after 24 hours is voided

rows.title: Tidy the facts that never found an order
rows.story: Facts still waiting for their order after 24 hours are escalated with an alert and never silently dropped. Facts older than 30 days are deleted.
rows.policy: Every sweep, escalate facts waiting over 24 hours and purge those older than 30 days

hotspots.text: All eight events are analytics-only. No other context reacts to a payment or refund event.
No alerting on declines, waiting facts, unpublished events or failed refunds. Only error log lines flag them.
A lost package whose shipment news never arrived is never refunded automatically. Its fact waits 24 hours, then is escalated.
A provider outage longer than the 24-hour lead lets a hold lapse. The next pass expires it without asking the provider.

delivery-promise.oneLine: Quotes delivery windows per speed tier, promises one to each shipment group, holds capacity for it, re-promises when the route breaks, then judges kept or broken.

rows.title: Quote delivery options for a destination
rows.story: A shopper sees what each shipment group can get, per speed tier, with a delivery window. A tier with no feasible route gets no offer, only the reason. The quote calls no other service.
reads: Node, lane, departure and wave copies
Stock per listing, net of promises

rows.title: Promise a shipment group
rows.story: At checkout a quoted offer becomes a provisional promise and holds one order of room on the node's pickup cutoff. The route is re-checked first; a route no longer feasible is refused as full.

rows.title: A pickup book fills up
rows.story: When a hold uses the last room before a node's pickup cutoff, the book announces it is exhausted. Later quotes find no room there.
rows.policy: Whenever a hold fills a pickup book, announce that the book is exhausted

then.does: keeps it as book pressure, a penalty when scoring paths

rows.title: Confirm the promise when the order is placed
rows.story: Checkout confirms each promise once the order is placed. The hold becomes a confirmed reservation. Confirming twice changes nothing.

rows.title: Catch a confirmation that checkout missed
rows.story: Normally checkout has confirmed already and nothing happens. A promise still provisional inside its hold is confirmed. If the hold has lapsed, it is only logged, never retried.
rows.policy: Whenever an order is placed, confirm its promises that are still provisional

rows.title: Cancel promises when an order is cancelled
rows.story: The cancelled groups' confirmed and at-risk promises are cancelled and their room goes back to the book. The same rule runs when an operator cancels one promise by hand.
rows.policy: Whenever an order is cancelled, cancel the promises of its cancelled groups

rows.title: Release a hold nobody confirmed
rows.story: A provisional promise that was not confirmed in time is released and its room returns to the book.
rows.policy: Every sweep, release provisional promises whose hold has lapsed

rows.title: Publish a new promise policy
rows.story: An operator publishes the next version of the promise rules: offer and hold lifetimes, capacity share, order deadlines per tier. A published version never changes.

rows.title: Keep the node profile copy
rows.story: Opening hours, handling time, pickup cutoffs and the throughput cap decide when a node can ship. Node status, lanes, service areas and regions are kept the same way, so quoting never calls out.
rows.policy: Whenever a node declares a profile revision, keep it if it is newer than the one held

rows.title: Keep the stock copy
rows.story: Quotes sell each owner's declared quantity minus units already promised that the figure may not include yet. Hidden listings and discontinued items ship nothing.
rows.policy: Whenever a listing's quantity changes, keep it unless it is older than the one held

rows.title: Keep the timetable copy
rows.story: A promise needs a pickup and legs with room. Departures are kept with their remaining room; delivery waves from last-mile-delivery are kept the same way.
rows.policy: Whenever a departure is scheduled, keep it with its remaining room

rows.title: Learn how long lanes really take
rows.story: A lane that runs late is quoted from what it really takes. The arrival also tells the late-risk check that the leg is done.
rows.policy: Whenever a load arrives, pair it with its departure to measure the transit time

rows.title: Flag promises on a cancelled departure
rows.story: Every confirmed promise whose route uses the cancelled departure is flagged at risk. Cancelled waves, failed or moved bookings, package exceptions, deferred induction and unsourceable groups flag the same way.
rows.policy: Whenever a departure is cancelled, flag the confirmed promises that ride on it

then.does: records the reason in the order's tracking view

rows.title: Spot routes that are running late
rows.story: A sweep checks confirmed promises: if a departure on the route is past its expected arrival, the promise is flagged at risk before the customer is let down. The flag is never cleared if the load arrives later.
rows.policy: Every sweep, flag confirmed promises whose route has a departure running late

then.does: records the reason in the order's tracking view

rows.title: Re-promise a later date, or give up
rows.story: The promise searches again for the same group, at its tier or slower, and moves later only. When nothing works it says so once, and the sweep keeps retrying.
rows.policy: Whenever a promise is at risk, search again and move it later if any route works

then.does: shows the new window, or cancels the group if unkeepable
applies the new window to the assignment

rows.title: Judge the promise: kept or broken
rows.story: Once the lock, the shipped packages and the deliveries are all known, the group is judged. On time is kept. Late, or a package lost or returned, is broken.
rows.policy: Whenever the last package is delivered, or one is lost or returned, judge the group

then.does: records the verdict and minutes late in the tracking view
records the outcome against the node's score

hotspots.text: A stale departure or wave copy can still be quoted. It is only refused when the promise is made, as a full book.
An order placed after its hold lapsed leaves a dead promise. The follow-up consumer only logs it and never retries.
A promise flagged as running late stays at risk even if the load arrives after all. Only the judgement closes it.
A lock on a full book keeps the capacity charge on the wrong node and only logs a warning. A metric is a follow-up.
An unkeepable promise stays at risk and is retried every sweep. It ends only when customer-ordering cancels the group.

opportunities.text: Measured-transit stretching could be widened to cover sort dwell and the last-mile wave. Deferred follow-up.
The reservation lag, now a constant, could become a promise policy field if operators need to tune it.
The consolidated-tier limits could become promise policy fields.

dock-scheduling.oneLine: Owns door time: who may use which dock door and when. It books, moves and cancels appointments, and follows the truck's real arrival and door from the yard.

rows.title: Book a time window at a dock door
rows.story: A carrier books a window at a door. It is refused if the door is closed or out of hours, the ASNs are unknown or already booked, the carrier is suspended, or another booking overlaps.

then.does: keeps a copy of the booking so the gate can match the arriving truck
adds the booking to its view of expected inbound demand
keeps a copy of inbound bookings
for an outbound booking with a cut-off, assigns the door to that load

rows.title: Move a booking to another window or door
rows.story: A carrier moves a booked appointment to a new window, or to another door. The same checks as a new booking apply. The event keeps the previous window and door.

then.does: updates its copy; frees held yard moves if the door changed
moves the booking in its expected inbound demand
updates the window and door in its copy

rows.title: Cancel a booking
rows.story: The carrier or the dock planner cancels a booked or checked-in appointment with a reason. The door window is freed.

then.does: marks it cancelled in its copy and frees held yard moves
records the cancellation in its expected inbound demand
marks it cancelled in its copy

rows.title: Report that a truck will be late
rows.story: A carrier reports when the truck will arrive. If that is later than the window plus the site's tolerance, the booking is flagged at risk. An ETA inside the tolerance clears an earlier flag.

rows.title: Cancel when every ASN of a booking is cancelled
rows.story: inbound-receiving announces that an ASN was cancelled. The ASN is marked cancelled in the local copy, and a booked inbound appointment whose ASNs are all cancelled is cancelled too.
rows.policy: Whenever the last ASN of a booked inbound appointment is cancelled, cancel the appointment

then.does: marks it cancelled in its copy and frees held yard moves
records the cancellation in its expected inbound demand
marks it cancelled in its copy

rows.title: Cancel when the gate turns a truck away
rows.story: The yard refuses a visit at the gate. If its appointment is still booked, it is cancelled with the reason 'turned away'. Any other state is ignored and counted.
rows.policy: Whenever the gate turns a visit away, cancel its booked appointment

then.does: marks it cancelled in its copy and frees held yard moves
records the cancellation in its expected inbound demand
marks it cancelled in its copy

rows.title: Note that the truck is at the gate
rows.story: The yard checks a truck in against a booking. The appointment becomes checked in and records whether the truck was early, on time or late.
rows.policy: Whenever a visit checks in against a booked appointment, record the arrival as early, on time or late

rows.title: Follow the truck to the door it really used
rows.story: If a trailer docks at a different door than the booked one, the real door wins and the booking moves there, even over another booking. Bookings it now overlaps are flagged at risk.
rows.policy: Whenever a trailer docks at another door than booked, the actual door wins

then.does: updates the appointment's door in its copy, so a receipt records the right door

rows.title: Close the booking when the trailer leaves the door
rows.story: When the yard reports the trailer undocked, the appointment is completed. If this news arrives before the gate check-in, the arrival is recorded as implicit.
rows.policy: Whenever a trailer leaves its door, complete the appointment it came for

rows.title: Sweep for carriers that never came
rows.story: A scheduler calls the sweep. Every booked appointment whose window plus the site's grace period has passed becomes a no-show. A no-show is final: a late carrier has to book again.
rows.policy: Every sweep, mark each booked appointment whose window and grace have passed as a no-show

then.does: marks it a no-show in its copy and frees held yard moves
records the no-show in its expected inbound demand
opens an exception case for the no-show, or updates the open one

rows.title: Declare when a site's doors operate
rows.story: A dock planner sets the operating hours of a site's doors. New hours that would strand an active appointment are refused.

rows.title: Close a door for a while
rows.story: A dock planner closes a door for a period, for example for repairs. It is refused if it overlaps another closure or covers an active appointment.

then.does: keeps the closure in its copy

rows.title: Reopen a closed door
rows.story: A dock planner lifts a scheduled closure early, and the door can be booked again.

then.does: removes the closure from its copy

rows.title: Add a carrier to the registry
rows.story: A planner records a carrier under its SCAC code. The registry is optional: a carrier that is not in it can still book. Changing its details later raises the same event again.

then.does: keeps a copy of the carrier registry

rows.title: Suspend a carrier
rows.story: A planner suspends a carrier. Bookings and moves that name it are refused until it is reinstated. Appointments it already has stay as they are.

then.does: keeps the carrier's suspended status in its copy

rows.title: Reinstate a suspended carrier
rows.story: A planner lets a suspended carrier book again.

then.does: keeps the carrier's active status in its copy

hotspots.text: Pickups from cut-offs are not built. The cut-off schedule is stored, but no outbound appointment is created, and the door rule and lead time are undefined.
A retired door blocks new bookings only. Appointments already on it are left untouched.
Appointment facts do not yet say whether an agent made the change. Only carrier facts carry that attribution so far.
The carrier registry is opt-in: a carrier that was never registered can still book. Only a suspended one is refused.

opportunities.text: A strict mode, where a named carrier must be registered to book, is a future per-site setting. It needs the registry populated first.
A carrier-connectivity context could translate these facts into partner formats. The ADR leaves that decision pending with the owner.

exception-management.oneLine: Gives every problem another context detects one owner: a case with severity, queue, deadline and root cause. Cases only ever start from a fact.

rows.title: Open a case for a missed cut-off
rows.story: A task is past its cut-off time. The first report opens a case with the severity, queue and deadline its policy sets. The report repeats at every sweep, so a repeat only adds to the count. A diverted or wrongly weighed package works the same way.
rows.policy: Whenever a task misses its cut-off, open a case, or count it on the case already open
reads: Handling policy for this kind of fact

rows.title: Triage a case
rows.story: An operator sets the severity and the queue of a case. It works on an escalated case too. A resolved case refuses it.

rows.title: Assign a case to an owner
rows.story: An operator gives the case an owner. It can be reassigned until the case is resolved.

rows.title: Resolve a case with a root cause
rows.story: An operator closes the case with a resolution code and a root cause. Resolved is final: later commands are refused, and a later matching fact only adds to the count, it never reopens the case.

rows.title: Set how a kind of problem is handled
rows.story: An operator declares the severity, queue, deadline in minutes and an optional auto-close rule for one kind of fact. Each declaration is a new version. Cases already open keep what they were opened with.

rows.title: Open a case for a work backlog
rows.story: wes-work-planning raises an alarm when the waiting work on a process path passes its threshold. The case is kept per path, and the alarm carries nothing but the path.
rows.policy: Whenever a backlog threshold is breached, open a case for that path, or count it on the open one
reads: Handling policy for this kind of fact

rows.title: Open a case for a late network order
rows.story: An order sent to another site is at risk of missing its acknowledgement deadline, or its hold was cancelled as orphaned. One case is kept per network order. The report repeats while the risk lasts.
rows.policy: Whenever a network order is at risk, open a case for it, or count it on the open one
reads: Handling policy for this kind of fact

rows.title: Open a case for an unexpected return
rows.story: A return arrives that nobody announced. One case is kept per return receipt.
rows.policy: Whenever an unexpected return is received, open a case for its receipt, or count it on the open one
reads: Handling policy for this kind of fact

rows.title: Open a case for a carton problem
rows.story: Receiving reports a carton that does not match its ASN. Missing, unexpected or mismatched cartons go to the problem-solve queue. Unlabelled or over-limit ones go to the receiving lead as low-priority information.
rows.policy: Whenever a carton discrepancy is raised, open one case per receipt, carton and kind, routed by kind
reads: Routes by kind of carton problem

rows.title: Open a case for a yard problem
rows.story: A trailer's seal differs from the one declared, a visit was turned away, a trailer overstayed, or a yard audit found a trailer missing. Each goes to the yard supervisor. A seal mismatch is the only high-severity one.
rows.policy: Whenever the yard reports a seal mismatch, rejected visit, long stay or audit finding, open a case
reads: Handling policy for this kind of fact

rows.title: Open a case for a missed appointment
rows.story: A carrier never showed for its dock appointment. One case is kept per appointment and goes to the dock planner.
rows.policy: Whenever an appointment is a no-show, open a case for it, or count it on the open one
reads: Handling policy for this kind of fact

rows.title: Open a case for a stock problem
rows.story: A bin count disagrees with the books, an item cannot be found, or a unit is put on hold. Each opens a case. A held unit gets exactly one, however often it is reported.
rows.policy: Whenever stock is in doubt or held, open a case for the bin or unit, or count it on the open one
reads: Handling policy for this kind of fact

rows.title: Open a case for a package that missed its truck
rows.story: A package was not loaded by its cut-off or by the trailer's departure. One case is kept per package, even if it misses a later load too. It goes to the problem solvers.
rows.policy: Whenever a package misses its load, open a case for the package, or count it on the open one
reads: Handling policy for this kind of fact

rows.title: Escalate a case past its deadline
rows.story: A sweep, once a minute by default, flags every open case that is past its deadline. Escalation is a flag set once per case. It never blocks work: the case can still be triaged, assigned and resolved.
rows.policy: Every sweep, any open case past its deadline and not yet flagged is escalated, once

rows.title: Close a case when the order is re-promised
rows.story: order-management re-promises an order. If an open cut-off case belongs to that order, and its policy has an auto-close rule whose time window has not passed, the case closes itself. No match leaves it open.
rows.policy: Whenever an order is re-promised, close the matching open case if its policy rule allows
reads: Handling policy for this kind of fact

rows.title: Close a held-stock case when the hold ends
rows.story: When held stock is released, returned to the vendor or scrapped, its case closes with the outcome in the note. Rework keeps the case open and counts another round.
rows.policy: Whenever held stock is released, returned or scrapped, close the case of that unit

hotspots.text: A fact whose kind has no declared handling policy is logged and skipped, not turned into a case.
Understaffed paths and stuck transfers are planned sources that are not built: they exist only on their producers' reporting streams.
A person cannot open a case by hand. Manual creation is left to a later version, and POST /exceptions is always refused.
Held units booked before the consumer first ran get no case. Nothing rebuilds history that was already dropped.
Routing works per kind of fact, not per detail. Another queue for one yard finding or one reason needs its own policy.

opportunities.text: labor-performance may read ExceptionResolved later, to relate cases to labour cost.
A missed-load case could auto-close when the package loads on its next load, if a later fleet decision wants that.
If repeated rework rounds become noise on a held-stock case, a rework-aware note is a possible follow-up.

facility-layout.oneLine: The warehouse map: sites, zones, aisles and coded location slots, plus the rules for what may legally sit where. Other contexts read it, none write it.

rows.title: Put a new building on the map
rows.story: An operator adds a physical facility under a short site code. Everything else on the map hangs below a site, so this comes first.

rows.title: Give a site its role in the network
rows.story: An operator states what part a site plays in the fulfilment network. Setting the role it already has changes nothing and raises no event.

rows.title: Declare what a site can send or receive
rows.story: An operator says whether a site may donate stock and whether it may receive stock. Every real change publishes a new numbered snapshot; repeating the same values does nothing.

then.does: keeps a copy of each site's capability; the highest revision wins

rows.title: Add a zone to a site
rows.story: An operator adds a zone inside an active site, with one temperature class and a hazmat flag. Other contexts use it to know what kind of area a slot sits in.

then.does: keeps the zone's hazmat and temperature class to check stows
keeps which site a zone belongs to, so a door knows its site
keeps the zone so yard spots and doors resolve to a site
keeps the zone for its copy of staging locations
keeps a copy of the layout
keeps a copy of the layout
keeps a copy of the layout

rows.title: Add an aisle to a zone
rows.story: An operator adds a corridor to an active zone, with its place in the walking order and whether it is one-way or two-way.

rows.title: Define a kind of slot
rows.story: An operator defines a reusable slot type such as a pallet rack, with its role (storage, dock, yard, work centre and others) and, where the role needs it, weight and volume limits.

rows.title: Say which slot kinds are allowed where
rows.story: An operator declares that a slot type is allowed or denied in the zones that match a condition, such as frozen zones. The rule is applied later, when each slot is registered.

rows.title: Register one location slot
rows.story: An operator registers a coded slot. It is refused if its site, zone or aisle is missing or retired, or if a placement rule forbids that slot type in that zone.

then.does: keeps inbound dock doors, ignores every other slot
keeps the slot; only dock doors can be booked
keeps yard spots and dock doors, ignores the rest
keeps its copy of staging locations
keeps the slot with its zone, hazmat and temperature class
counts storage positions and work stations
keeps a copy of the layout
keeps a copy of the layout
keeps a copy of the layout

rows.title: Load a whole building at once
rows.story: An operator submits a table of slots. Missing sites, zones and aisles are created on the way and each row succeeds or fails alone. One summary says how many rows went in.

rows.title: Declare how a slot is handled
rows.story: An operator says whether a slot takes single items, cases or pallets. The slot must exist and must not be retired.

then.does: sets the bin's handling unit in its copy; the last write wins

rows.title: Pin a slot to the floor plan
rows.story: An operator records where a slot sits and how big it is, in metres. Distance questions then use real positions instead of an estimate.

then.does: keeps the slot's position in its copy of the layout

rows.title: Draw an aisle's walking line
rows.story: An operator sets the centreline along which an aisle is walked. The travel graph uses it for measured distances.

rows.title: Connect two aisles
rows.story: An operator declares that two aisles of the same zone can be crossed at a given bay. Walking distances can then go from one aisle to the other.

rows.title: Record a wall or other fixed structure
rows.story: An operator records a wall, column, office or conveyor on a site, so a floor plan can be drawn to scale. It is not a place where stock can sit.

rows.title: Keep site capability facts fresh
rows.story: A site's capability is only published when it changes, so a reader would see it age out. On a fixed interval the context republishes each active site's current values as a new revision.
rows.policy: Every interval, republish the current capability of each active site that has declared one

then.does: keeps the site's capability copy fresh instead of letting it go stale

rows.title: Retire a slot for good
rows.story: An operator permanently retires a slot. There is no way back, and its code is never reused. Other contexts stop offering it for new work.

then.does: removes the door from its dock-door list
removes the door, so no new bookings; existing ones stay
marks the slot retired in its copy
stops offering the location for new stows
takes the slot out of its storage count
retires the slot in its copy of the layout
retires the slot in its copy of the layout
retires the slot in its copy of the layout

hotspots.text: Retiring is one-way and nothing can set a structure to 'under maintenance'. A mistaken retirement cannot be undone through the API.
Distance between two zones with no recorded positions is refused with an error, not estimated. The ADR calls this the point most likely to be revisited.
Fixed structures are stored and published, but the travel graph does not yet treat them as obstacles.
Cross-aisle distances are always estimated from the aisles' spacing. The walkway's own geometry is left to a later phase.
Aisle lines, cross-aisles and fixed structures are published but nobody consumes them yet.

opportunities.text: Work-planning contexts could ask for travel distances through a future lookup port. The ADR leaves this as a separate decision.
A to-scale floor plan mixing zones with and without geometry is deferred until a consumer needs printed floor plans.

fulfillment-execution.oneLine: Runs work on the floor: tasks wait in a pool, stations claim and complete them, and picked orders are packed, weigh-checked and manifested.

rows.title: Create a task from released work
rows.story: wes-work-planning releases a unit of work. A task is created once per release, from the process path catalogue, and put in the pool for stations to claim. A task with a known location is announced to the pool.
rows.policy: Whenever work is released, create a task for it from the process path catalogue

then.does: learns of the open task, so it can advise stations what to work next

rows.title: Keep the product handling copy
rows.story: Sealing a package checks that the hazard classes of its items can travel together. The classes come from a copy of product-master's classification, so sealing never calls out. An unclassified item never blocks.
rows.policy: Whenever a SKU is classified, keep the classification if its version is newer

rows.title: Keep the pack levels copy
rows.story: A pick scan is checked against the packs product-master declares. Each and case barcodes resolve to a SKU and a number of units. Retired levels are kept as ended.
rows.policy: Whenever a pack level is declared or retired, update the pack view

rows.title: Claim the next task
rows.story: A station asks for work and is given the best-fitting pending task, on a lease so that only one station holds it. Advice from task-interleaving only breaks ties inside a priority band.

then.does: marks the task as taken, so it stops advising it

rows.title: Confirm a scan against a pick
rows.story: The operator scans an each or a case barcode against a pick task. The scan is checked against the pack view and the picked quantity is counted in eaches.

rows.title: Form a pick walk
rows.story: With batching switched on, a station gets one walk of several pick tasks with the same cut-off, up to a maximum and with no hazard clashes. The first task is the one a plain claim would give.

rows.title: Complete a task
rows.story: The station that holds the lease completes the task. The completion carries what downstream needs: the work unit, the order reference and, for a relocation, the SKU, bins and quantity.

then.does: marks the unit of work as done
books the stock move behind a confirmed pick or a relocation
records how long the task took and who did it
learns the capacity actually observed

rows.title: Close a pick walk
rows.story: When the last open task of a walk is completed, the walk completes in the same step, with its member count and walking time.
rows.policy: Whenever the last open task of a walk is completed, complete the walk

rows.title: Record a transfer step
rows.story: Completing a task that belongs to a stock transfer also reports that transfer's pick, dispatch or arrival.

then.does: keeps the transfer facts to follow each transfer

rows.title: Arrive at the rebin wall
rows.story: A picked line arrives at its order's consolidation slot. When the last required line is there, one PACK task is created, once.

rows.title: Seal a package
rows.story: The packer scans the contents and seals the package. An empty carton is never sealed, and items whose hazard classes clash are refused.

rows.title: Pass the weigh check
rows.story: The sealed package is weighed against its expected weight. Within tolerance, a label is applied and the package is manifested for shipping.

then.does: takes the manifested package into its own view
closes the promise feedback for the order line
keeps a copy of the manifest

rows.title: Fail the weigh check
rows.story: Outside tolerance, the discrepancy is reported and the package is diverted instead of labelled. Both facts reach exception-management, so someone owns the problem.

then.does: opens a case for the package

rows.title: Free tasks whose lease lapsed
rows.story: A scheduled job returns claimed tasks whose lease ran out to the pool, so another station can take them. If that was the last open task of a walk, the walk is abandoned.
rows.policy: Every sweep, a claimed task whose lease has lapsed goes back to the pool

rows.title: Report missed cut-offs
rows.story: A scheduled job reports every open task whose cut-off has passed. It changes nothing on the task and reports the same task again on each pass.
rows.policy: Every sweep, any open task past its cut-off is reported as missed

then.does: opens a case, or counts the repeat on the open one
re-promises the order

rows.title: Count an item picked (never raised)
rows.story: The model has a fact for each item picked, with an encoder for the analytics stream. No use case raises it: picking is tracked per task, from claim to completion.
rows.policy: Whenever an item is picked, copy it to the analytics stream (nothing raises it yet)

hotspots.text: A station can claim work without being checked in. Check-in is recorded but does not gate a claim.
ItemPicked is defined and has an encoder, but no use case raises it. Picking is tracked per task, not per item.
The sort lane is decided for each package, but no conveyor or sorter system exists to act on it.
A missed cut-off is reported again on every sweep, so consumers must count it once.
Rebin arrival has no real event source yet, only a manual entry point. The two rebin events never leave the process.

opportunities.text: A real sorter system could take the sort lane as its own fact. That integration is not built.
A rebin location model (which bin holds a line) and cartonization are left out of the rebin design.
Records of sent events are never purged. A retention sweep is named as a follow-up.

inbound-receiving.oneLine: Receives deliveries at the dock: from an announced ASN to a closed, counted receipt.

rows.title: Announce a delivery
rows.story: A supplier announces what is coming. The ASN is only accepted if every SKU on it is a product the warehouse knows.

then.does: feeds its ASN view so a door can be planned
feeds its inbound views

rows.title: Cancel an announcement
rows.story: The supplier withdraws the announcement. It only works while nothing has been received yet.

then.does: cancels a booking when all its ASNs are cancelled

rows.title: Keep the appointments copy
rows.story: The dock booking lives in dock-scheduling. Here a read-only copy follows its bookings, reschedules and door changes, so receiving never has to ask.
rows.policy: Whenever an inbound appointment is booked, cancelled or moved, update the local copy

rows.title: Keep the product list
rows.story: Every product that product-master registers becomes a known SKU, so an ASN can be checked without a live call.
rows.policy: Whenever a product is registered, add its SKU to the known SKUs

rows.title: Keep the dock-door list
rows.story: Only inbound dock doors matter here. facility-layout announces every location slot; receiving keeps the doors it can use.
rows.policy: Whenever a slot is registered, keep it only if it is an inbound dock door

rows.title: Open a receipt at the door
rows.story: The truck is at the door. Dock staff open a receipt for the ASN, with or without an appointment, and the ASN moves to Receiving.

then.does: feeds its inbound views

rows.title: Count a line
rows.story: Dock staff count what is on the pallet and record it as Good or Damaged. Only Good units become stock.

then.does: books the Good units as staged stock

rows.title: Receive by scan
rows.story: Dock staff scan a carton label. An accepted carton books its contents; a refused scan is not an error, it becomes a recorded finding.

then.does: creates or links the carton's container
keeps a copy of the carton and the finding
handles the discrepancy

rows.title: Close the receipt
rows.story: Dock staff close the receipt. It reports every difference against the ASN, flags cartons that never showed up and sends the receiving advice.

then.does: keeps a copy of the closed receipt
feeds its inbound views

rows.title: Complete the ASN
rows.story: When the receipt closes, the ASN closes with it, in the same transaction. Nobody has to remember to do it.
rows.policy: Whenever a receipt closes, close its ASN in the same transaction

rows.title: Measure dock-to-stock: the gate
rows.story: The yard reports when the truck reached the gate. That is the start of the dock-to-stock clock.
rows.policy: Whenever a visit checks in, store the arrival and check whether the evidence is complete

rows.title: Measure dock-to-stock: the shelf
rows.story: inventory-storage reports when a carton was stowed. When the last Good carton is on the shelf, the dock-to-stock time is known.
rows.policy: Whenever a container is stowed, store the stow and check whether the evidence is complete

rows.title: Chase a late advice
rows.story: A periodic sweep looks for open receipts whose receiving advice is past its deadline and raises an overdue notice.
rows.policy: Every sweep, any open receipt past its advice deadline raises an overdue notice

hotspots.text: No tolerance policy: every over-receipt is reported, never silently accepted. A tolerance is a later decision.
Damaged units are counted but have no quarantine flow. They are not booked as stock.
If inventory-storage rejects a line, it skips and logs. The receipt stays the source of truth, nothing compensates.
The deprecated appointment routes stay in the API pending a decision, although dock-scheduling owns appointments.

opportunities.text: The receiving advice has no reader yet. Partner connectivity could send it back to the supplier.

inventory-storage.oneLine: The stock ledger of a site: books received goods, stows them into bins, reserves and picks them, moves and counts them, and settles held stock and transfers.

rows.title: Book a received line as staged stock
rows.story: inbound-receiving reports a line counted as Good. Its units become staged stock: counted, but not usable until someone stows them. Return lines staged by returns-processing are booked the same way.
rows.policy: Whenever a Good line is received, book its units as staged stock, once per event

rows.title: Stow stock into a bin
rows.story: Inventory control scans the item and then the bin. Hazmat and temperature-sensitive products must go to a fitting zone, and hazard classes that clash may not share a bin. Stowed stock becomes usable.

then.does: re-checks whether the SKU's pick face is running low

rows.title: Turn a received carton into a container
rows.story: inbound-receiving scans a sealed carton. It becomes a container with its own license plate, but only for units the ledger has already counted, whichever of the two messages arrives first.
rows.policy: Whenever a sealed carton is received, link it to a container once its units are counted

rows.title: Stow a sealed case
rows.story: Inventory control scans the case and then a case or pallet bin. The case's eaches become usable stock in that bin. Stowing again into another bin of the same site moves the case.

then.does: uses the stow to finish its dock-to-stock timing

rows.title: Break a sealed case into loose eaches
rows.story: Inventory control opens a stowed case on purpose. Its eaches move to loose stock in a chosen bin, with the same total, and the container is left empty. It is never done implicitly by a pick.

rows.title: Hold a damaged line out of stock
rows.story: A line received as Damaged is never usable. It becomes a held unit that waits for a decision, and its units stay out of usable stock.
rows.policy: Whenever a Damaged line is received, hold it out of usable stock

rows.title: Decide what happens to held stock
rows.story: Inventory control decides: release it back to the normal flow, return it to the vendor, scrap it, or keep it held for rework. A release books the units as staged stock again.

rows.title: Reserve stock for an order
rows.story: An order system asks to bind a quantity of usable stock to a demand. Pick faces are drawn first, in a fixed order. A repeat of the same request is recognised, and an unused reservation times out.

then.does: lowers the usable stock it observes for the SKU

rows.title: Revoke a reservation
rows.story: A reservation is cancelled and its quantity returns to usable. Timeouts are only noticed when a reservation is read: if it had already timed out, the timeout is recorded instead.

then.does: raises the usable stock it observes for the SKU

rows.title: Confirm the picks of a finished task
rows.story: When a pick task completes, the reservation of that order line is used up and the stock leaves. Events without a line number are counted instead, and the order's last pick confirms everything.
rows.policy: Whenever a pick task completes, confirm the reservation of that order line

rows.title: Move stock between bins
rows.story: A finished relocation or replenishment task moves stock between two bins of one site, in one step. The move carries a reason and a reference, and can also be made by hand over the REST route.
rows.policy: Whenever a relocation or replenishment task completes, move the stock it names

then.does: tracks slot-plan progress from moves made for slotting
closes the request when the move is a replenishment

rows.title: Count a bin
rows.story: Inventory control counts what is in a bin. A shortfall marks whole units as unlocated, an overage is only reported, and every count is recorded.

then.does: opens a case for a count mismatch and for each unlocated item

rows.title: Hold origin stock for a transfer
rows.story: Network planning asks this site to give up stock for a transfer line. The stock is held and the answer, allocated or rejected with a reason, is recorded exactly once per line.
rows.policy: Whenever planning requests a transfer allocation, hold the stock and record the outcome once

then.does: moves the transfer on, as allocated or rejected

rows.title: Release the hold of a cancelled transfer
rows.story: If a transfer is cancelled after allocation, planning asks for the hold to be released. The stock returns to usable, or the hold is found already gone, and either way the transfer settles.
rows.policy: Whenever planning asks to release a transfer allocation, free the hold and record the outcome once

then.does: marks the transfer cancelled

rows.title: Count a transfer arrival
rows.story: The destination site counts what arrived against a transfer line. Over and short counts are recorded as they are, not absorbed. An arrival nobody allocated is recorded as an exception.

then.does: records the counted arrival and any difference

rows.title: Stow a transfer into destination bins
rows.story: The counted arrival is stowed into bins of the destination site, and the quantities must add up exactly. Only now does the destination's usable stock rise, once per transfer line.

then.does: records the stow for the transfer

hotspots.text: There is no sweeper for timed-out reservations. An unread one keeps its stock out of usable until someone reads it.
A stow into a bin facility-layout never announced is allowed. Fragile, oversized and high-value products have no placement rule.
Short picks are not modelled: a task carries no quantity, so a confirmed line is picked in full.
A cycle-count overage is reported but never reconciled. That needs a separate receiving or audit process.
The check that stops two identical reservations is best effort. Two requests arriving at the same moment can both pass.

opportunities.text: Quality inspection could place holds. Reasons for pending checks and suspect stock are already accepted for later producers.
Lot and expiry are carried on containers, but first-expired-first-out picking is out of scope for now.
Transfer allocation still draws stock in storage order. Making that order deterministic is a recorded follow-up.

labor-performance.oneLine: Scores every finished warehouse task against the engineered time allowed for it, and reports how each associate and task type is performing.

rows.title: Set the time allowed for a task type
rows.story: An industrial engineer sets how many seconds a task type (pick, pack, slam) should take. A task type with no open standard gets its first one.

rows.title: Set a time for a handling unit, with a team lift
rows.story: The engineer can set a separate time for handling each, case or pallet units. A case standard may also say that a heavy case is a team lift with its own time.

rows.title: Tighten or loosen a standard
rows.story: When a standard is already open, the new one closes it at the same instant. History is never overwritten, so old tasks keep the yardstick they were scored with.
rows.policy: Whenever a standard is already open for the task type and unit, close it as the new one starts

rows.title: Score a finished task
rows.story: When fulfillment-execution reports a task as completed, it is scored against the standard that was in force at that moment, and the associate's idle time since the previous task is worked out.
rows.policy: Whenever a task completes, record its performance exactly once

then.does: keeps a running average task time and idle share per task type, for planning

rows.title: Keep the performance report up to date
rows.story: Each score and each standard change is counted into an hourly report per task type, which supervisors read together with a freshness check. The report has no command of its own.
rows.policy: Whenever a performance or standard event is published, count it once into its task type and hour

hotspots.text: The default idle-gap cap of one hour is a judgment call, not a measured shift length. Operators with other shifts must override it.
fulfillment-execution does not yet send the handling unit or case weight, so unit standards and team lifts never apply to live tasks.
Task types this context does not model (for example REBIN) arrive unclassified: they are counted but never scored.
No access control inside the service: the standards and scorecard routes are open to anyone who can reach it.

opportunities.text: fulfillment-execution could add the handling unit and case weight to TaskCompleted, which would switch the unit standards on.
Standard changes could be published for other contexts to read; today only the scoring facts are shared.

last-mile-delivery.oneLine: Runs the final leg: delivery waves at a station, packages taken in when loads arrive, partner routes, delivery attempts, retries and returns.

rows.title: Keep the list of delivery stations
rows.story: Node-topology announces every node. Only delivery stations matter here; a wave or a partner can be set up only for a station that is on this list.
rows.policy: Whenever a node is registered, keep it only if it is a delivery station

rows.title: Keep the stop of each labelled package
rows.story: When a label is issued, the package's stop key and order assignment are kept. Packages for one address share a stop, so they take one place in a wave.
rows.policy: Whenever a label is issued, keep the package's stop key; a label without a usable key is ignored

rows.title: Schedule a delivery wave
rows.story: A station planner opens a wave: an induction cut-off, a delivery window and how many stops it can take. Packages already waiting at the station are taken into it, oldest first.

then.does: adds the wave to its copy so promises can use it
adds the wave to the network copy its search uses

rows.title: Take in packages when a load arrives
rows.story: When a load reaches a delivery station, each package goes into the earliest wave that still accepts it. A package no wave accepts waits at the station and a deferral is announced.
rows.policy: Whenever a load reaches a delivery station, put each package on the earliest open wave or defer it

then.does: updates the room left on the wave; a deferred package flags its promise as at risk
updates the room left on the wave in its network copy

rows.title: Declare what a stop costs
rows.story: A station planner declares the cost of one stop on a wave that is still running. Order-sourcing adds it to the cost of the routes it compares.

then.does: uses it as the wave's per-stop cost when comparing routes

rows.title: Close induction on a wave
rows.story: A station planner stops taking packages into a wave, so routes can be planned on a fixed set of packages.

rows.title: Cancel a wave
rows.story: A station planner cancels a wave that is still open. Its packages move to the next eligible wave in the same step, or wait at the station.

then.does: flags promises whose route used the wave as at risk
marks the wave as cancelled in its network copy

rows.title: Contract a delivery partner
rows.story: A station planner signs up a delivery service partner for a station, with the van capacity of its routes.

rows.title: Deactivate a delivery partner
rows.story: A station planner deactivates a partner. It gets no new routes; routes already planned are not re-checked.

rows.title: Plan a partner's route in a wave
rows.story: A station planner gives a partner a numbered list of stops from a wave whose induction is closed. The route must fit the van, use only packages of the wave and keep one address in one stop.

rows.title: Dispatch a wave
rows.story: A station planner sends the wave out. Packages that no route holds are moved to the next wave, and a wave with no route completes at once.

rows.title: Start a route
rows.story: An operator starts a planned route of a dispatched wave. Every package goes out for delivery, and each stop gets an arrival window of up to two hours inside the wave's delivery window.

then.does: records an out-for-delivery scan and keeps the arrival window of each package

rows.title: Record a delivery attempt
rows.story: The driver records for each package whether it was delivered or failed. A package is delivered at most once, and the route completes when every package has an attempt.

then.does: records a delivered or failed-delivery scan for the package

rows.title: Retry a failed delivery, or send it back
rows.story: After a failed attempt the package goes on the next eligible wave. After the third failure it is not retried: a return to sender starts.
rows.policy: Whenever an attempt fails, place the package on the next wave unless it was the third failure

then.does: marks the package as returned to sender

rows.title: Flag a drop-off point that keeps failing
rows.story: Each attempt updates the profile of its stop. After two failed visits for not-home or access problems within 60 days, the point is flagged for the packages affected. A flag changes no route.
rows.policy: Whenever an attempt is recorded, update the stop's profile; two failed visits flag the point

then.does: keeps the flag on every package of the stop

hotspots.text: A route stays out for delivery until every package has an attempt. If the driver skips one, the route and its wave stay open.
Deactivating a partner re-checks nothing: routes already planned keep the partner and the van capacity read at planning time.
Failure reasons are free text and the optional outcome detail is dormant until a client sends it, so delivery-point flags depend on clients adopting it.
The arrival window is spread evenly across the wave's window: there is no travel-time or position data to refine it.
Service-area assignments are kept but no decision reads them yet.

opportunities.text: Entrance, parking and locker knowledge for a drop-off point is left to a later item that needs its own model change.

linehaul-transportation.oneLine: Plans the trucks and flights between nodes, books each locked order's package on a pickup, and tracks loads from dispatch to arrival.

rows.title: Define a lane's weekly schedule
rows.story: A planner sets the weekly template of a lane: for each slot the cut-off, departure and arrival times and how many packages fit. Redefining replaces the slots; departures already planned stay.

rows.title: Retire a lane's schedule
rows.story: A planner retires the schedule of a lane. No new departures are planned from it; departures already planned are not cancelled.

rows.title: Keep two weeks of departures planned
rows.story: At start and then every interval, every active lane schedule is expanded into departures for the next 14 days. A rerun adds only what is missing.
rows.policy: Every interval, plan the departures missing from the next 14 days of every active schedule

then.does: adds the departure to its copy so promises can use it
adds the departure to the network copy its search uses

rows.title: Plan pickups when a vendor centre goes live
rows.story: A vendor-run centre gets a pickup departure for each of its declared cut-offs, over 14 days. Pickups are re-planned when its profile changes or a lane opens, whichever arrives last.
rows.policy: Whenever a centre is activated, revised or gets a lane, plan its pickups from its cut-offs

then.does: adds the pickup to its copy so promises can use it
adds the pickup to the network copy its search uses

rows.title: Stop pickups when a centre leaves service
rows.story: When a node is suspended or retired, its future pickups are cancelled, and every package booked on them is moved to the next pickup or reported as failed.
rows.policy: Whenever a node is suspended or retired, cancel its future pickups

then.does: flags promises whose route used the pickup as at risk
marks the pickup as cancelled in its network copy

rows.title: Cancel a departure
rows.story: A planner cancels a departure that has not left. Every package booked on it moves to the next pickup from the same origin, or the booking is reported as failed.

then.does: flags promises whose route used the departure as at risk
marks the departure as cancelled in its network copy

rows.title: Change a departure's capacity
rows.story: A planner resizes a departure that has not left. It cannot go below what is already booked.

then.does: updates the room left on its copy of the departure
updates the room left on its copy of the departure

rows.title: Book a package when the order locks
rows.story: When a group locks on a node, one package is booked on its pickup. If that pickup is full, closed or gone the booking moves to the next pickup, or fails. A merged package books only once.
rows.policy: Whenever a group locks, book one package on its pickup, or the next one, or report a failure

then.does: points the locked group at the new pickup; a failed booking changes nothing there
flags the promise as at risk and skips the departure that was left

rows.title: Keep the expected volume
rows.story: Each release tells linehaul which node and planned pickup a group is heading for. A reassignment or cancellation only updates this record; nothing is booked before the lock.
rows.policy: Whenever a group is released, reassigned or cancelled, update its expected volume record

rows.title: Keep the tracking numbers
rows.story: Shipping-and-tracking issues the labels. Linehaul keeps each tracking number on the group's record; a voided label removes its number but keeps the booking.
rows.policy: Whenever a label is issued or voided, add or remove its tracking number on the group's record

rows.title: Open a load on a departure
rows.story: An operator opens the load that will ride a departure that has not left. A departure has at most one load.

rows.title: Add a package to the load
rows.story: An operator scans a package onto an open load. A package can be on only one open load, and the load cannot exceed the departure's capacity. On a truck or flight (not a pickup) the package also takes a seat.

rows.title: Close the load
rows.story: An operator closes the load; the departure closes with it. No package can be added afterwards.

rows.title: Dispatch the load
rows.story: An operator sends a closed load on its way. The load and its departure are recorded as departed.

then.does: records a departure scan for each tracking number
starts timing the trip to measure real transit time

rows.title: Receive the load at its destination
rows.story: An operator receives a departed load at its destination. The load and its departure are recorded as arrived.

then.does: takes in each package when the load reaches a delivery station
records an arrival scan for each tracking number
completes the measured transit time and notes the arrival

hotspots.text: A booking that fails leaves the locked group without a seat. Order-sourcing only records it; delivery-promise flags the promise as at risk.
If order-sourcing cancels after the lock, the package stays booked on its departure until the departure leaves.
A closed lane cancels nothing: departures already planned on it stay until a planner cancels them by hand.
There is no metric for the unsent-event backlog, consumer lag or the horizon roll, and no alert on parked failed messages; they are read from the database and logs.

network-fulfillment.oneLine: The seam to the external retail network: answers its purchase orders in time, tells it what the building can ship, and reports what the dock received.

rows.title: Take a purchase order and hold the stock
rows.story: A new purchase order is recorded and its products are translated to our SKUs. order-management holds the stock and promises a ship date. If the date is feasible, the whole order is accepted.
rows.policy: Whenever a poll finds a new purchase order, record it and start its answer clock

then.does: is told the whole order is accepted; it is settled later

rows.title: Refuse an order we cannot take
rows.story: One unknown product, or a ship-by date the building cannot meet, refuses the whole order. Any stock already held is freed and the network is told no, with the reason.
rows.policy: Whenever a purchase order has an unknown product or an infeasible date, refuse all of it

then.does: is told no, with the reason (unknown listing or cannot meet ship-by)

rows.title: Settle an accepted order
rows.story: The network confirms or refuses an answer later. On success the order is acknowledged and the held stock is released. On failure the hold is freed and the order is refused.
rows.policy: Every pass, ask the network about each accepted order: success settles it, failure refuses it, pending waits

rows.title: Confirm that an order shipped
rows.story: Once acknowledged, an order can be confirmed as shipped. It is normally triggered when outbound-shipping reports the load as shipped; an operator can also do it by hand. The network gets a label request first.

then.does: is sent the label request and then the shipment confirmation

rows.title: Report an order past its answer deadline
rows.story: A sweep finds orders still unanswered after their deadline and reports each one on every pass. It never changes the order itself.
rows.policy: Every sweep, report each unanswered order that is past its deadline, and leave the order unchanged

then.does: opens an exception for the order, or adds to the one already open

rows.title: Refuse an order nobody answered in time
rows.story: A separate sweep refuses orders whose deadline passed unanswered, and frees the held stock if there is a hold. An overdue order is never answered late.
rows.policy: Every sweep, refuse each unanswered order that is past its deadline and free its held stock

rows.title: Free a hold nobody decided
rows.story: order-management never times out a held order, so this context does. An open hold well past the deadline is cancelled and reported. The order's own state is left alone.
rows.policy: Every sweep, cancel any open hold that is past its deadline plus a grace period

then.does: opens an exception for the order, or adds to the one already open

rows.title: Keep the cutoff schedule copy
rows.story: process-path-management announces process paths and their cutoff schedules. A local copy of the cutoffs and path cycle times lets offers and the site profile be worked out without a live call.
rows.policy: Whenever a path or its cutoff schedule changes, update the local copy

rows.title: Keep the path capacity copy
rows.story: wes-work-planning announces how much capacity is left on each path before each cutoff. A local copy lets offers and cutoff ceilings be worked out without a live call.
rows.policy: Whenever a path's remaining capacity changes, update the local copy

rows.title: Work out what we could offer
rows.story: For each known SKU the offer is the lower of the stock usable now and what the paths can still handle before the next feasible cutoff. Unknown capacity falls back to stock.
rows.policy: Every pass, work out an offer per SKU from usable stock and the capacity before the next cutoff

rows.title: Tell the network how the building works
rows.story: In live mode, each site's cutoffs, handling time and order ceilings are derived from the local copies and declared to the network. A new revision is sent only when the content changed.
rows.policy: Every pass, declare each site's operating profile to the network, but only if it changed

then.does: learns each site's cutoffs, handling time and order ceilings

rows.title: Tell the network what we can ship
rows.story: In live mode, the saved offers become an inventory feed per site. The feed is sent when it changed, and repeated at most hourly when it did not.
rows.policy: Every pass, send each site's offers for the items the site lists, when they changed

then.does: learns how many of each listed item the site can ship

rows.title: Announce a seller shipment to receiving
rows.story: In live mode, shipments the network says are on their way are recorded. Each one is registered in inbound-receiving as an expected delivery before the truck arrives. Failures are retried with a growing wait.
rows.policy: Whenever a poll finds a shipped seller shipment, record it and register an expected delivery

rows.title: Keep a copy of the receipts at the dock
rows.story: inbound-receiving announces each accepted carton, each carton finding and each closed receipt. A local copy keeps only the deliveries this context announced, so the result can be reported later.
rows.policy: Whenever a receipt closes, keep it with its cartons and findings, but only for our own deliveries

rows.title: Report what the dock received
rows.story: Each closed receipt is turned into a per-carton result: received, damaged, missing or unexpected, with any findings. It is sent to the network exactly once per shipment.
rows.policy: Every pass, report each closed receipt not yet reported, retrying with a growing wait

then.does: is told what arrived, carton by carton, with the findings

hotspots.text: The deadline warning fires only after the answer deadline has passed. The decision record says it should fire as the deadline approaches.
If releasing the held stock fails after an order settles, nothing retries it: the order no longer counts as awaiting settlement.
The network is always told one package per order, because the shipped-load fact carries no per-order package count yet.
Remaining capacity is counted as one order per unit, so a declared cutoff ceiling can be too high until the network corrects it.
Dock findings with no carton label (unknown product, unlabelled carton) cannot be reported to the network. They are only logged.

opportunities.text: outbound-shipping could add a per-order package count to its shipped-load fact. The consumer already tolerates it, so the real count would flow.
Pack levels from the network's listings could be declared to product-master once the open question of which side owns a product code is settled.

network-inventory-planning.oneLine: Plans moving stock between warehouses: advises, then runs an approved transfer from stock reservation through pick, dispatch and arrival.

rows.title: Keep the site capability copy
rows.story: facility-layout says which sites may send or receive transfers. Here a local copy follows it, and a newer revision replaces the older one, so planning never has to ask.
rows.policy: Whenever a site's capability changes, replace its row if the revision is newer

rows.title: Keep the demand copy
rows.story: order-management reports the units each order line needs from a site. A local copy keeps the newest fact per line. A removed line counts for nothing.
rows.policy: Whenever an order line's demand changes, keep its newest version; a removed line counts for none

rows.title: Keep the capacity plan copy
rows.story: warehouse-planning publishes capacity plans. A local copy keeps the newest plan for each plan id. A plan with no site is left out.
rows.policy: Whenever a plan for a site is published, keep the newest version of it

rows.title: Set the rebalance rules
rows.story: An operator writes the policies that say which SKUs may move, and the lanes between sites. The scheduled rebalance plans only from these catalogues. Lanes are set the same way.

rows.title: Try out transfers without committing
rows.story: An operator submits positions, policies and lanes and gets advisory proposals back. A simulation can instead use the local copies. Nothing is reserved or published.

rows.title: Approve a transfer and ask for stock
rows.story: An operator approves a proposal. It is checked against the local copies, and refused if a fact is missing or stale. SKUs sold in cases move in whole cases. inventory-storage is then asked for the origin stock.

then.does: reserves the origin stock and answers allocated or rejected

rows.title: Release the pick once stock is held
rows.story: inventory-storage reports the stock reserved. The transfer becomes allocated and the pick work is released in the same step, so an allocated transfer never lacks its pick work.
rows.policy: Whenever origin stock is reserved, mark the transfer allocated and release its pick work

then.does: creates the transfer pick as a work unit referring to the transfer

rows.title: Give up when stock cannot be held
rows.story: inventory-storage refuses the reservation, with a reason from a fixed list. The transfer is marked unfulfillable and ends there.
rows.policy: Whenever origin stock cannot be reserved, mark the transfer unfulfillable with the reason

rows.title: Cancel a transfer
rows.story: An operator cancels with a reason. Before any stock is held the transfer is cancelled at once. If stock is already reserved, a release is requested first. From picking onwards the cancel is refused.

then.does: lets go of the origin reservation and reports back

rows.title: Finish a cancel once the hold is gone
rows.story: inventory-storage confirms the origin reservation is released, or was already gone. Either way the hold no longer exists, so the transfer is cancelled for good.
rows.policy: Whenever the origin reservation is released, mark the cancelling transfer cancelled

rows.title: Release the dispatch once picked
rows.story: fulfillment-execution reports the pick, possibly short. The picked quantity is recorded and dispatch work is released for exactly that quantity.
rows.policy: Whenever the pick completes, record the picked quantity and release the dispatch work

then.does: creates the dispatch as a work unit referring to the transfer

rows.title: Mark the transfer in transit
rows.story: fulfillment-execution reports that the goods left the origin. The transfer moves to in transit. No work is released for this step.
rows.policy: Whenever dispatch completes, mark the transfer in transit

rows.title: Mark the transfer arrived
