rows.story: inventory-storage reports the receipt staged at the destination. A work-driven arrival fact from fulfillment-execution may also exist. Whichever comes first moves the transfer to arrived; the other is skipped.
rows.policy: Whenever the first arrival signal comes, mark the transfer arrived

rows.title: Close the transfer once stowed
rows.story: inventory-storage reports the goods stowed at the destination, with where they went. The transfer is received and its journey ends.
rows.policy: Whenever the stow is confirmed, mark the transfer received and keep where the stock went

rows.title: Flag transfers that are stuck
rows.story: A periodic check compares each open transfer with a time limit for its state and reports the ones past it. It only reports: it never cancels or changes a transfer.
rows.policy: Every check, report each open transfer that has stayed too long in its state

rows.title: Run a scheduled rebalance
rows.story: On a schedule, the planner works from the local copies and the operator's catalogues, and records how many proposals it made and how many it rejected. It never approves anything.
rows.policy: Every run, plan proposals from the local copies and record the outcome, without approving any

hotspots.text: A transfer can no longer be cancelled once picking has started. The stock is moving, and there is no damage or short-pick flow yet.
If the dispatch path is not configured, the dispatch work is withheld and nothing releases it later. The transfer waits in picked.
The scheduled rebalance cannot see stock positions, so it plans only from site capability, demand and catalogues.
The stuck-transfer check only reports. Nothing retries or recovers a stuck transfer on its own.
The dwell report shows a transfer's age at each step, not the time spent in a state. A true dwell time needs a new field.

opportunities.text: If a sibling context ever publishes stock positions, they could be kept locally and the scheduled pass could plan from real stock.
Adding a dwell-seconds field to the state-change event would give a true time-in-state report.

node-performance.oneLine: Grades each fulfillment node on what it actually did over the last 7 and 30 days, and tells the network when a grade changes.

rows.title: Remember a purchase order's deadlines
rows.story: When a vendor is sent a purchase order, this context keeps its ship-by and acknowledge-by deadlines. Later facts are judged against them. Nothing is counted yet.
rows.policy: Whenever a purchase order is issued, keep its ship-by and acknowledge-by deadlines

rows.title: Fill in the ship-by deadline
rows.story: The shipment confirmation repeats the ship-by deadline. It is merged into what is already known, so either message can arrive first. The vendor's own ship time is not used.
rows.policy: Whenever a vendor confirms a shipment, complete the purchase order's ship-by deadline

rows.title: Judge an acknowledgement
rows.story: A vendor accepts or rejects a purchase order. The answer counts as late if it comes in the last tenth of the time allowed. Without the order's deadlines it cannot be judged and is retried.
rows.policy: Whenever a purchase order is accepted or rejected, record how timely the answer was

rows.title: Count an expired order
rows.story: A purchase order ran out of time without an answer. That counts against the node as a late acknowledgement, always.
rows.policy: Whenever a purchase order expires, record a late acknowledgement

rows.title: Judge a handover against the ship-by time
rows.story: The carrier took a package from the node. It counts as on time if the handover is not after the purchase order's ship-by time; the exact boundary is on time.
rows.policy: Whenever a package is handed over, record whether it beat the ship-by time

rows.title: Count a kept promise
rows.story: delivery-promise says a delivery promise was kept. That counts in the node's favour.
rows.policy: Whenever a promise is kept, record it for the node

rows.title: Count a broken promise, if it is the node's fault
rows.story: A broken promise only counts against the node when the cause is the node's: late, late handover, vendor refusal or an unanswered order. A lost or returned package is the network's, and is ignored.
rows.policy: Whenever a promise is broken, record it only for a cause the node is responsible for

rows.title: Count an inventory feed
rows.story: offer-availability applied a stock feed from the node. The gaps between feeds show how fresh the node's stock numbers are.
rows.policy: Whenever a node's inventory feed is applied, record the time of the feed

rows.title: Note when an inbound shipment left
rows.story: A seller's shipment to the node has been shipped. Its ship time is kept, first one wins, to compare with the receipt later. It is shown on reads but never graded.
rows.policy: Whenever an inbound shipment is shipped, keep its shipped time

rows.title: Note what an inbound receipt found
rows.story: The node reports what it received for a shipment. Carton counts are kept, the first report wins, and the receipt is joined to the shipment when both are known. Shown on reads, never graded.
rows.policy: Whenever an inbound receipt is submitted, keep its carton counts

rows.title: Note the node's declared profile and do nothing
rows.story: The node's declared profile arrives and is only logged as seen. A grade comes from observed facts, never from what a vendor declared.
rows.policy: Whenever a node declares its profile, record that the message arrived and change nothing

rows.title: Recompute the grades
rows.story: A periodic run recomputes every scorecard that has new facts or facts that left the window. A node needs 50 observations to get an A to D grade; below that it stays provisional and nothing is published.
rows.policy: Every run, recompute the due scorecards and announce a changed grade or metric

then.does: keeps the 30-day grade; B pads handling time, C and D skip a pickup option
keeps the 30-day grade and adds a cost penalty for B, C and D

rows.title: Warn when a metric gets worse
rows.story: When a graded node's metric crosses its bound in the wrong direction between two graded runs, a breach is raised, one per metric. It goes to analytics only, nobody in the network reacts.
rows.policy: Whenever a graded scorecard changes, raise a breach for each metric that crossed its bound

rows.title: Suspend or reinstate a node's fast tiers
rows.story: On the 7-day card, a graded on-time handover rate below 90% suspends the node from same-day and next-day. Three separate days at 95% or better reinstate it. Each flip is announced once per tier.
rows.policy: Every run, flip a node's fast-tier eligibility when its 7-day on-time rate says so

then.does: keeps each node's eligibility per tier and leaves ineligible nodes out of fast-tier offers

hotspots.text: A handover or answer that beats its purchase order is retried, then parked in a failure queue. Nothing re-processes that queue.
Declared profile next to measured behaviour is not modelled: the profile message is received and ignored.
The broken-promise causes the model names differ from what delivery-promise sends; in practice only LATE counts against a node.
Inbound accuracy mixes node and seller causes until they are separated. It is informational and never graded.
After a stuck event hits its send-attempt cap, a later event of the same scorecard can reach consumers first.

opportunities.text: If inbound timeliness should count towards a grade, a new decision is needed: the facts would become observations.
A node directory or a declared-versus-measured view could use the profile messages already received.
A compacted counter form is the follow-up if one node's volume grows by orders of magnitude.

node-topology.oneLine: Owns the physical shape of the retail network: its buildings (nodes), the lanes between them, the regions, and which delivery station serves each postal prefix.

rows.title: Define a region
rows.story: A planner names a region with a short unique code. Every node and every postal-prefix assignment must belong to a region that exists.

then.does: keeps a copy of the region
keeps a copy of the region

rows.title: Register a node
rows.story: A planner, or the vendor-connectivity service for a vendor's building, registers a building. It starts as Proposed. The kind of building decides who may run it and what it can do.

then.does: starts tracking the node as Proposed, so no listing is suppressed yet
keeps a copy of the node's type and region
keeps the node only if it is a delivery station
keeps the node and re-plans pickups on lanes that end at it

rows.title: Declare how a node operates
rows.story: The vendor or a planner declares opening hours, handling time, pickup cutoffs and a throughput cap. Each declaration is a new numbered revision that never overwrites an earlier one.

then.does: re-plans pickup departures from the node's cutoffs
keeps handling time, cutoffs and cap when the revision is newer
keeps the node's carton limits to check shipments against
acknowledges the event and changes nothing

rows.title: Put a node into service
rows.story: A planner activates a Proposed or Suspended node. A fulfillment centre must first have a cutoff and a handling time above zero.

then.does: marks the node sellable and restores listings suppressed for it
generates the node's pickup departures
marks the node active for promising

rows.title: Suspend a node
rows.story: A planner pauses an active node and must give a reason. Its lanes and postal prefixes are left as they are; other contexts must treat them as unusable.

then.does: suppresses the node's live listings
cancels the node's future pickups
marks the node suspended

rows.title: Retire a node for good
rows.story: A planner retires an active or suspended node. Retired is final: any later command on that node is refused.

then.does: suppresses the node's live listings
cancels the node's future pickups
marks the node retired in its copy

rows.title: Open a lane between two nodes
rows.story: A planner opens a ground or air lane. Both ends must be active, the pair of building types must be allowed, and no identical lane may already be open.

then.does: keeps the lane and re-plans pickups at its origin
adds the lane to the network graph it searches
adds the lane to the network graph it searches

rows.title: Declare what a lane costs
rows.story: A planner states the cost, in cents, of moving one package across an open lane. A newer declaration replaces the previous one. A lane never declared on publishes nothing.

then.does: keeps the latest cost per lane and prices candidate paths in cents

rows.title: Close a lane
rows.story: A planner closes an open lane. A closed lane is never reopened; a new lane gets a new identity.

then.does: schedules no new departure on the lane
marks the lane closed in its network graph

rows.title: Assign a postal prefix to a delivery station
rows.story: A planner decides which delivery station serves a postal prefix. A later assignment must carry a higher version; the prefix takes the station's region.

then.does: keeps the assignment when its version is higher
keeps the assignment when its version is higher
keeps the prefix-to-station assignment

hotspots.text: A suspended or retired node keeps its open lanes and assigned prefixes. Nothing closes or reassigns them; readers must treat them as unusable.
A lane never costed reads zero but publishes nothing, so readers cannot tell 'free' from 'unknown' by the number alone.
A profile may name a time zone other than its node's. The model never says whether they must match.
After repeated failed sends (20 by default) an event is skipped, so a later event of the same node or lane can overtake it.

opportunities.text: A declared lane cost is the first step toward costing paths in money. A measured cost per departure could later refine it.

offer-availability.oneLine: Keeps the catalogue of items, where each item is offered (listings) and how many units each node says it has, and hides listings that cannot be sold.

rows.title: Add an item to the catalogue
rows.story: Merchandising creates an item with its size, weight, handling flags and an optional barcode. A barcode already held by another item or pack level is refused.

then.does: keeps a copy of the item as active
keeps the item's size, weight and handling flags
marks the item as catalogued, so it can be added to a cart
knows the item exists, so it can be priced
records the item as active

rows.title: Declare how an item is packed
rows.story: Merchandising declares a pack level (each, inner, case or pallet) with its barcode and units. A new barcode at a level replaces the old one, which is retired in the same step.

then.does: keeps the pack level to check shipment contents
keeps the pack level in its packaging view

rows.title: Retire a pack level
rows.story: Merchandising retires the active pack level. The level stays on the item, so a document that names its barcode still resolves.

then.does: marks the pack level retired in its copy
marks the pack level retired in its copy

rows.title: Offer an item from a node
rows.story: Merchandising offers an item from one node. The listing starts live only if the node is active, the item is not discontinued and the seller, if any, is not suspended. Otherwise it starts hidden.

then.does: keeps a copy of the listing
keeps a copy of the listing
keeps a copy of the listing, so it can check feed lines

rows.title: Apply a stock feed for a node
rows.story: A vendor reports quantities for one node. Each line sets a listing's quantity; a full feed zeroes the listings it leaves out. A feed older than the last applied one is set aside and changes nothing.
reads: Last applied feed time of the node

then.does: keeps the quantity unless it is older than the one it holds
keeps the quantity of the listing
records that the node sent a feed

rows.title: Discontinue an item
rows.story: Merchandising withdraws an item for good. Every listing of the item is hidden in the same step, and a listing hidden for this reason is never put back.

then.does: stops new additions to carts; lines already in carts stay
withdraws the item's price if it has an active one
retires the item's content
marks the item discontinued in its copy
marks the item discontinued in its copy

rows.title: Keep a copy of node status
rows.story: node-topology announces each new node. Here it is noted as Proposed, so listings created for it start hidden until it goes live.
rows.policy: Whenever a node is registered, note it as Proposed unless it is already known

rows.title: Show listings again when a node goes live
rows.story: When a node is activated, its hidden listings come back. One stays hidden if its item is discontinued or its seller is suspended, and it then shows that reason.
rows.policy: Whenever a node is activated, restore the listings hidden because the node was unavailable

then.does: marks the listing sellable again
marks the listing sellable again

rows.title: Hide listings when a node leaves service
rows.story: When a node is suspended, or retired for good, every live listing on it is hidden. Retired is final.
rows.policy: Whenever a node is suspended or retired, hide all its live listings

then.does: marks the listing suppressed
marks the listing suppressed

rows.title: Hide a suspended seller's listings
rows.story: When a seller is suspended, every live listing the seller owns is hidden. A listing already hidden for a stronger reason keeps that reason.
rows.policy: Whenever a seller is suspended, hide every live listing the seller owns

then.does: marks the listing suppressed
marks the listing suppressed

rows.title: Show a reinstated seller's listings again
rows.story: When a seller is reinstated, the listings hidden for that seller come back, unless the node is still unavailable or the item is discontinued. Then they stay hidden for that reason.
rows.policy: Whenever a seller is reinstated, restore its listings unless another reason still holds

then.does: marks the listing sellable again
marks the listing sellable again

rows.title: Create listings from received seller stock
rows.story: When a seller's shipment is received at a node, each item without a listing for that seller there gets one, at zero quantity. Items that cannot be matched are skipped and counted, never an error.
rows.policy: Whenever a seller's shipment is received, create the seller's missing listings on that node

then.does: keeps a copy of each new listing
keeps a copy of each new listing

hotspots.text: A full feed rewrites every listing of a node in one transaction. No throughput or lock-time figure has been measured.
While the node-status consumer lags, listings keep their last state and the service still reports ready.
No contract test checks the downstream readers of these events. The reader list comes from the network map, not from this repo.
Shipments received before seller-inbound added item lines never become listings. They need a manual listing or a later shipment.

opportunities.text: Measure feed apply time, the share of stale lines and how long hiding takes after a node leaves service. Proposed, not built.

order-management.oneLine: Takes customer orders, reserves stock for every line, promises a ship date and releases the work. It also holds orders for other contexts and re-promises when plans slip.

rows.title: Keep the product classification copy
rows.story: product-master classifies each product (handling tags, temperature, hazard class). A local copy lets intake pick a process path without a live call. This runs only when switched on.
rows.policy: Whenever a product is classified, keep its newest classification

rows.title: Keep the process paths and cutoffs copy
rows.story: process-path-management announces process paths and the cutoff schedule. A local copy lets intake choose a path and promise a cutoff without a live call.
rows.policy: Whenever a path or its cutoff schedule changes, update the local copy

rows.title: Keep the path capacity copy
rows.story: wes-work-planning says how much work each path can still take before each cutoff. A local copy lets the promise avoid cutoffs that are already full.
rows.policy: Whenever a path's remaining capacity changes, update the local copy

rows.title: Keep the planned capacity copy
rows.story: warehouse-planning publishes capacity plans and shortages. A local copy lets an order response show which shortage windows overlap its promise. It changes no promise.
rows.policy: Whenever a capacity plan or shortage is published, store its window; a draft never overwrites a published one

rows.title: Take an order and release it
rows.story: The order is saved and every line gets a stock reservation. A ship date is promised from the paths' cutoffs. Reserved lines are released as work, so the customer gets a promise at once.

then.does: turns each released line into a work unit on its process path
keeps a copy of the allocated lines for later return checks
adds the order to its expected demand

rows.title: Take an order that cannot be fully reserved
rows.story: A line with too little stock is backordered and the pass goes on. A ship-complete order releases nothing until every line is reserved. If inventory-storage fails part-way, what was reserved is kept and the failure is reported.

then.does: creates work only for the lines that were released

rows.title: Retry a stuck allocation
rows.story: An operator retries the backordered lines of an order. Lines that can now be reserved are reserved and released. Unlike intake, a hard failure here is returned to the operator.

then.does: turns each newly released line into a work unit

rows.title: Hold an order for another context
rows.story: A calling context asks for stock held, not released, with a ship-by time and a fulfillment site. The order must be ship-complete. It gets a promise date, or none if the deadline cannot be met.

then.does: keeps the line's demand at its site in a local copy

rows.title: Release a held order
rows.story: The caller decides to go ahead. Reservations are checked again, because they can lapse. The reserved lines are released as work, and a ship-complete order releases nothing if a line was lost.

then.does: turns each released line into a work unit on its process path

rows.title: Cancel an order
rows.story: Reservations are given back and every line is cancelled. It is refused once any line has been released, and nothing is changed in that case.

then.does: drops the cancelled lines from its demand copy, for orders with a site
drops the cancelled lines from its demand copy, for orders with a site

rows.title: Re-promise when a task misses its cutoff
rows.story: fulfillment-execution reports a task past its cutoff, or a package manifested. The promise of that line's shipment group is worked out again. A new event is raised only if the promise moved.
rows.policy: Whenever a task misses its cutoff, work out the promise of its shipment group again

then.does: closes the open exceptions it matches to this order

rows.title: Re-promise when a package misses its load
rows.story: outbound-shipping reports a package that missed its load. Every shipment group of that order is promised again. Each group whose promise moved raises its own event. This runs only when switched on.
rows.policy: Whenever a package misses its load, work out the promise of every group of its order again

rows.title: Mark lines shipped when the load leaves
rows.story: outbound-shipping reports a load as shipped, naming its orders. Released lines of those orders become shipped. The result stays a local fact. This runs only when switched on.
rows.policy: Whenever a load is confirmed shipped, mark the released lines of its orders as shipped

rows.title: Confirm a release from the work unit
rows.story: When work is released, a pending confirmation is opened per line. wes-work-planning's work unit for that line settles it. This runs only when switched on, and is off by default.
rows.policy: Whenever a work unit is created for a released line, mark that line's release confirmed

rows.title: Flag a release nobody confirmed
rows.story: A housekeeping sweep finds released lines still unconfirmed after the timeout and flags each once. It only reports. Nothing is cancelled, re-released or retried. This runs only when switched on.
rows.policy: Every sweep, flag each released line still unconfirmed after the timeout, once

hotspots.text: Once any line is released the order can no longer be cancelled, and work already released is not clawed back.
Release is fire-and-forget. Without the opt-in confirmation, this context never learns whether wes-work-planning created the work.
A line that is never confirmed is only flagged. No automatic reaction exists, and compensation would need its own decision.
A held order has no timeout inside this context. It relies on its caller, or network-fulfillment's sweep, to release or cancel it.
Path capacity and cycle time are per path for the whole fleet, not per site, because upstream contracts carry no site.

opportunities.text: Per-site path capacity could be used once wes-work-planning and process-path-management carry a site on their contracts.
A dedicated reply event from wes-work-planning could replace watching WorkUnitCreated to confirm a release.

order-sourcing.oneLine: Chooses which fulfillment node ships each group of an order, releases it at the right time and tracks it from release to delivery.

rows.title: Queue a shipment group
rows.story: When an order is placed, each shipment group gets an assignment and the best node is picked; a same-day group is released at once. If no node can serve the group in time, it is marked unsourceable so the promise can be revised.
rows.policy: Whenever an order is placed, queue one assignment per shipment group and pick its best node

then.does: flags the promise as at risk when no node can serve the group
keeps the reason on the order tracking view

rows.title: Release a group to its best node
rows.story: A sweep releases every group whose release time has come. The node is re-checked against fresh copies first, and the release records why this node was chosen.
rows.policy: Whenever a queued group's release time is due, re-check the best node and release the group to it

then.does: issues a purchase order to the node
notes the planned pickup; nothing is booked yet
adds the released lines to its demand view

rows.title: Release one shopper's packages together
rows.story: If the shopper chose the consolidated delivery day and a merge limit is published, queued groups with the same key ride on the first group's release. The merge never moves the node.
rows.policy: Whenever a due consolidated group has queued mates with the same key, release them as one

then.does: receives one purchase order carrying the lines of every merged group

rows.title: Move a queued group to a better node
rows.story: A network planner, or the sweep, asks for a fresh search for a group that is still queued. If another node is now better the group moves; if none is left it becomes unsourceable.

then.does: updates its view of the group's node

rows.title: Publish a sourcing policy
rows.story: A planner sets the cross-region surcharge, how far above the cheapest route the choice may drift to stay in region, and how many groups may merge. Every publish makes the next version; nothing changes until one exists.

rows.title: Lock the group when the node accepts
rows.story: When the node accepts the purchase order, the group is locked on that node and its pickup departure. After that it can no longer be moved or cancelled.
rows.policy: Whenever the node accepts the purchase order of the pending release, lock the group on that node

then.does: moves the capacity hold to the locked node and pickup, then re-judges the promise
marks the group as in fulfilment
books one package on the pickup departure, or moves it to the next one

rows.title: Try another node after a refusal
rows.story: If the node rejects the purchase order or lets it expire, that node is excluded and the group is searched again. A merged release breaks up and each group is searched on its own.
rows.policy: Whenever a node rejects or lets a purchase order expire, skip that node and search again

then.does: updates its view of the group's node
flags the promise as at risk when no node is left

rows.title: Record the shipment
rows.story: When the node confirms that the purchase order shipped, the group is marked shipped with its tracking numbers, and a merged release ships all its groups.
rows.policy: Whenever the node confirms a shipment, mark the group shipped with its tracking numbers

then.does: marks the group shipped and stores the tracking numbers
records the packages of the group to judge the promise
captures the payment of the group

rows.title: Record the delivery
rows.story: Each delivered package is remembered. The group counts as delivered only when its last package arrives.
rows.policy: Whenever a package is delivered, record it; the last package delivers the group

rows.title: Cancel a group before it locks
rows.story: A cancelled order cancels its groups while they are queued, released or unsourceable. A locked group, or a member of a merged release, refuses the cancellation and the order keeps it.
rows.policy: Whenever an order is cancelled, cancel its groups that are not locked and refuse the others

then.does: cancels the purchase order of a released group
updates its view of the group
removes the group's lines from its demand view
lets go of the payment hold for the group
confirms the cancellation, or keeps the group when refused

rows.title: Re-check a group after a promise change
rows.story: When delivery-promise revises a promise, the group gets the new deadline and its exclusions are reset. A merged release that no longer fits the window is withdrawn and its groups are searched again.
rows.policy: Whenever a promise is revised, apply the new deadline and search again if the group is still queued

then.does: cancels the purchase order of the withdrawn release

rows.title: Follow a moved pickup
rows.story: If linehaul moves a booking to another departure, the locked group points at the new pickup. The node never changes. A failed booking changes nothing here.
rows.policy: Whenever a booking moves to another departure, point the locked group at the new pickup

rows.title: Keep the network map
rows.story: Nodes, their profiles and status, lanes, regions and service areas come from node-topology. Order-sourcing keeps a copy so a search never needs a live call.
rows.policy: Whenever a node, lane, region or service area changes, update the local network copies

rows.title: Keep the departures copy
rows.story: Linehaul announces departures, capacity changes and cancellations. A route can only start on a departure that this copy still shows as usable.
rows.policy: Whenever a departure is scheduled, resized or cancelled, update the local departures copy

rows.title: Keep the delivery waves copy
rows.story: Last-mile delivery announces its waves, capacity changes, cancellations and per-stop costs. A route ends on a wave of the destination's station.
rows.policy: Whenever a wave is scheduled, resized, cancelled or priced, update the local waves copy

rows.title: Keep the availability copy
rows.story: Offer-availability reports what each node can ship. A node only qualifies when every line of the group is listed, not suppressed and in stock.
rows.policy: Whenever a listing's stock changes, update the local availability copy

hotspots.text: After a promise revision withdraws a merged release, the vendor may still accept the old purchase order: a duplicate pick and ship of the other groups' goods.
If the pickup departure of a locked group is cancelled, no transition handles it: the departures copy changes and nothing else.
An acceptance that arrives after the group was cancelled is only logged, so the vendor may still ship.
A group released at the latest pickup has no slack: after a refusal there may be no later wave, so it becomes unsourceable.
FulfillmentConstraintRevised has no consumer declared in any spec yet.

opportunities.text: A split surcharge and a single-node preference are not built. Revisit when sourcing plans across the groups of one order.

outbound-shipping.oneLine: Turns manifested packages into loads for a carrier cutoff, tracks them onto the truck, and confirms the shipment when the truck leaves.

rows.title: Keep the cutoff times
rows.story: process-path-management announces each site's daily cutoffs. Shipping keeps the latest schedule as a local copy, so it can tell which cutoff a package belongs to.
rows.policy: Whenever a site's cutoff schedule changes, replace the local copy for that site

rows.title: Plan a load for a manifested package
rows.story: A packed parcel is manifested. Shipping works out which cutoff it must make, joins the open load for that cutoff or plans a new one, and expects the package on it.
rows.policy: Whenever a package is manifested, join the open load for its cutoff or plan one

rows.title: Drop a diverted package
rows.story: If fulfillment diverts a package, it is short-shipped at once with the reason DIVERTED, so it cannot hold up the closing of its load.
rows.policy: Whenever a package is diverted, short-ship it so its load can still close

rows.title: Give the load a door
rows.story: dock-scheduling books an outbound appointment for a cutoff. The appointment is always kept, and its door goes to the open load of that cutoff.
rows.policy: Whenever an outbound appointment names a cutoff, give its door to the open load

rows.title: Start loading when the trailer docks
rows.story: The yard reports a trailer at a door. If a planned load uses that door, the trailer is attached to it and loading starts.
rows.policy: Whenever a trailer docks at a load's door, attach it and start loading

rows.title: Stage a package
rows.story: A dock operator scans a package into a staging spot, ready for its truck. Only a staging location of the package's own site is accepted.

rows.title: Load a package onto the truck
rows.story: A dock operator scans the package at the door. It is accepted only for the load it belongs to, and only through that load's assigned door.

rows.title: Take a package back off the truck
rows.story: An operator removes a loaded package from its load. It goes back to staged, with an optional reason. A package that already shipped can no longer be unloaded.

rows.title: Close the load
rows.story: The supervisor closes the load once every package is loaded or short-shipped with a reason. Closing can list the packages to short-ship.

rows.title: Reopen a closed load
rows.story: The supervisor puts a closed load back to loading so work can continue. A load whose shipment is already confirmed never reopens.

rows.title: Cancel a planned load
rows.story: The supervisor cancels a load that never got going. It is refused once packages are assigned to it; those must be short-shipped and the load closed instead.

rows.title: Confirm the shipment when the truck leaves
rows.story: Only the yard's departure fact makes a shipment real. A departure with a seal, for a closed load, ships its loaded packages and tells order-management which orders left.
rows.policy: Whenever a trailer leaves with a closed load and a seal, confirm the shipment

then.does: marks the lines of the shipped orders as shipped

rows.title: Issue the bill of lading
rows.story: The moment the shipment is confirmed, one bill of lading is issued for the load, with the carrier, the yard's seal, the package count and the total weight.
rows.policy: Whenever a shipment is confirmed, issue its bill of lading in the same step

rows.title: Flag packages left behind at departure
rows.story: If the truck leaves before the load was closed, nothing is confirmed. Every package that was not loaded is flagged as having missed its load, once, and a supervisor decides.
rows.policy: Whenever a trailer leaves an unclosed load, flag each package not loaded

then.does: re-promises the order: recomputes its delivery promise
opens one case for the missed package

rows.title: Sweep for packages that missed the cutoff
rows.story: An outside scheduler calls the sweep after a cutoff. Every package still expected or staged on an open load past its cutoff is flagged, and a re-run flags nothing twice.
rows.policy: Every sweep, flag each package not loaded on an open load past its cutoff

then.does: re-promises the order: recomputes its delivery promise
opens one case for the missed package

rows.title: Void a bill of lading
rows.story: A supervisor voids an issued bill of lading and gives a reason. The shipment itself is not undone.

hotspots.text: A truck that leaves before its load is closed never confirms the shipment, even if the load closes right after. Only a new departure would.
No bill of lading exists before departure, so a carrier that needs it in hand before leaving cannot be served yet.
An appointment that arrives before its load exists only saves a copy. The door is not assigned when the load is planned later.
Nothing in this repository schedules the missed-load sweep. An outside scheduler has to call it.
An order split over two loads yields two shipment events. Whether the retail network accepts a partial confirmation is still unchecked.

opportunities.text: The yard could react to loading started, load closed and load reopened. That consumer is deferred until the yard contract merges.
Pallets, load sequencing and a master bill of lading are deliberately deferred; version one ships packages only.

pick-face-replenishment.oneLine: Watches forward pick faces against a min/max rule and asks for stock to be moved from the fullest reserve bin, then closes the request when the move is recorded.

rows.title: Declare a min/max rule for a pick face
rows.story: A planner sets the minimum, maximum and case multiple for one SKU at one site. Changing a rule needs the version the planner last saw.

rows.title: Ask for stock when a face runs low
rows.story: inventory-storage reports a new bin level. If the pick face of that SKU is now at or below its minimum, a request is raised to move stock from the fullest reserve bin.
rows.policy: Whenever a bin level changes, keep it and re-check that SKU's pick face

then.does: plans one REPLENISH work unit for the request

rows.title: Close the request when the stock has moved
rows.story: inventory-storage records a relocation tagged as replenishment. If it matches an open request, the request is completed with the quantity actually moved.
rows.policy: Whenever a replenishment move is recorded for an open request, complete that request

rows.title: Check a whole site by hand
rows.story: A planner re-runs detection for every pick face of a site. Faces that already have an open request are left alone, so running it twice raises nothing new.

then.does: plans one REPLENISH work unit for the request

rows.title: Ask for a replenishment by hand
rows.story: A planner raises a request for one SKU, optionally with a quantity. It is refused if there is no pick face, no rule or no source stock, or if a request is already open.

then.does: plans one REPLENISH work unit for the request

rows.title: Follow the case size from product-master
rows.story: A rule can take its multiple from the SKU's case size instead of a typed number. When the case size changes, such rules get a new multiple. A retired case size flags them stale.
rows.policy: Whenever a case size is declared, keep it and re-derive the multiple of rules that follow it

rows.title: Follow the approved slot plan
rows.story: slotting-optimization approves a new forward map. Requests whose face no longer holds that SKU are cancelled, and new or moved faces are checked for stock.
rows.policy: Whenever a newer slot plan is approved, replace the forward map and cancel requests it drops

then.does: withdraws REPLENISH work that is still pending
plans one REPLENISH work unit for the request

rows.title: Keep the layout copy
rows.story: facility-layout announces zones and locations, and later retires some. Here a copy tells which bins are pick faces and which are reserve bins.
rows.policy: Whenever a zone or location is registered or decommissioned, update the layout copy

rows.title: Cancel a request
rows.story: A planner cancels a request that is still open. A completed or cancelled request is final and cannot be cancelled again.

then.does: withdraws REPLENISH work that is still pending

rows.title: Remove a rule and its open requests
rows.story: A planner removes the rule of a SKU. In the same step every open request for that SKU at the site is cancelled.

then.does: withdraws REPLENISH work that is still pending

hotspots.text: A bin never seen reads as level 0, so a face whose level has not arrived yet can get an unnecessary URGENT request.
Requests only become floor work if wes-work-planning opts in and the REPLENISH path is seeded; cluster state was not checked.
A partial fill leaves the face below its maximum. The next detection raises a fresh request once the first is closed.
Until a bin changes, its stock level is unknown because inventory-storage has no backfill. Detection then finds no source bin.

opportunities.text: A demand-cover rule (days of cover from demand) is planned as a later policy kind behind the same shape as min/max.
Velocity-derived min/max, multi-SKU faces, reserve-to-reserve consolidation and travel-aware source choice are listed for later ADRs.

pricing.oneLine: Owns what a shopper pays: list prices and sales per item, delivery charges, a tax table, and the binding price quote a checkout is built on.

rows.title: Price a new item
rows.story: A merchandiser sets the first list price of a catalogue item. The item must already be known and not discontinued, and the amount must be in the one configured currency.

then.does: shows the price on the product page and marks the item purchasable
keeps the item's current price for its cart estimate

rows.title: Change a list price
rows.story: A merchandiser changes the standing price of an item. A price change is announced only if what shoppers see really moved, and a sale price must stay below the new list price.

then.does: updates the price on the product page
updates the item's current price for its cart estimate

rows.title: Schedule a sale
rows.story: A merchandiser plans a sale window with a price below the list price. Windows of one item never overlap. If the window is already open the new price is announced now, otherwise later.

then.does: updates the price on the product page
updates the item's current price for its cart estimate

rows.title: Cancel a sale
rows.story: A merchandiser cancels a planned or running sale. Cancelling the running sale puts the price back to the list price and announces it; cancelling a future one announces nothing.

then.does: puts the list price back on the product page
puts the list price back in its cart estimate

rows.title: Withdraw a price
rows.story: A merchandiser takes an item's price off. A withdrawn price is final: it cannot be changed, scheduled or quoted again, and the item stops being purchasable.

then.does: marks the item as no longer purchasable
clears the item's price, so it is no longer purchasable

rows.title: Publish delivery charges
rows.story: A merchandiser publishes a new delivery charge schedule: one charge per delivery speed, with an optional free-delivery threshold. It replaces the current one and its version must be higher.

then.does: replaces the delivery charges used in its cart estimate

rows.title: Publish the tax table
rows.story: A merchandiser publishes a new tax table: rates by destination postal-prefix band, never overlapping. It replaces the current table and its version must be higher.

then.does: replaces the tax rates used in its cart estimate

rows.title: Quote a checkout
rows.story: When a checkout opens, it asks for a binding quote for the frozen cart. The quote fixes goods, delivery, tax and total, is valid for 15 minutes and comes back in the same reply.

rows.title: Keep the catalogue list
rows.story: offer-availability announces every new catalogue item. Pricing keeps a copy of which items exist, so a price can be set without a live call.
rows.policy: Whenever a catalogue item is created, record it as known and active

rows.title: Withdraw the price of a discontinued item
rows.story: When an item is discontinued, its price is withdrawn automatically, in the same step that records the discontinuation. An item that was never priced only updates the copy.
rows.policy: Whenever an item is discontinued, mark it so and withdraw its active price

then.does: marks the item as no longer purchasable
clears the item's price, so it is no longer purchasable

rows.title: Announce prices when a sale starts or ends
rows.story: A sweep looks for sale windows that opened or closed since the price was last checked and announces the new price. Re-running the same boundary announces nothing.
rows.policy: Every sweep, an item whose sale started or ended announces its new price

then.does: updates the price on the product page
updates the item's current price for its cart estimate

rows.title: Let old quotes expire
rows.story: A sweep marks issued quotes as expired once their 15 minutes are over. Nothing is announced: a quote past its time already reads as expired.
rows.policy: Every sweep, any issued quote past its expiry time becomes expired

hotspots.text: A price cannot be set before the item is known here. The request is refused and the merchandiser has to retry once the catalogue event arrives.
A withdrawn price is final and cannot be revived. How to sell the item again is documented as an open question.
A price can move between the cart's estimate and the checkout. Only the binding quote is final, and it lasts 15 minutes.

opportunities.text: Coupons and promotions are a later phase; today a sale window is the only way to discount an item.
The tax table is synthetic. Real tax calculation is meant to come from a bought tax engine later.

process-path-management.oneLine: Keeps the warehouse's catalogue of process paths and each site's carrier cut-off schedule, and tells the rest of the fleet whenever either changes.

rows.title: Define a new process path
rows.story: An operator adds a path to the catalogue: its name prefix, the skills it needs, its p95 cycle time and which demand sources may feed it. A path id is never reused, even after retirement.

then.does: adds the path to its catalogue copy, so released work for it is accepted and gets its required skills
adds the path to its catalogue copy, so work can be planned onto it
adds the path to its catalogue copy, so shift plans and assignments can name it
adds the path, with its cycle time and eligibility, to the copy it uses to route orders
adds the path's cycle time to the copy it uses for capacity figures

rows.title: Revise a process path
rows.story: An operator changes an active path's prefix, skills, cycle time, eligibility or intake. If nothing actually changed, nothing is announced. The full new definition is sent, never a diff.

then.does: replaces its copy of the path definition
replaces its copy of the path definition
replaces its copy of the path definition
replaces its copy, so the next delivery promise uses the new cycle time and eligibility
replaces the cycle time it uses for capacity figures

rows.title: Retire a process path
rows.story: An operator retires a path for good. It is refused while any site's cut-off schedule still lists the path, so the operator revises those schedules first.
reads: Sites whose schedule lists the path

then.does: removes the path from its catalogue copy
removes the path from its catalogue copy
removes the path from its catalogue copy
removes the path from its copy, so no order is routed onto it
removes the path from its capacity copy

rows.title: Publish a site's cut-off schedule
rows.story: An operator sets, or replaces in full, a site's carrier cut-off times. Every path a cut-off lists must be active. An identical schedule changes nothing and announces nothing.

then.does: replaces the site's cut-off windows it uses to promise delivery times
replaces the site's cut-offs it uses for capacity figures
replaces its copy of the site's cut-off schedule
stores the site's cut-offs as a view; it books no appointment from them yet

rows.title: Replay every active path at start-up
rows.story: When the service starts, it announces the current definition of each active path again. This way a consumer that rebuilds its catalogue from scratch never misses a path whose first event has aged out.
rows.policy: Whenever the service starts, announce every active path again

then.does: a fresh instance rebuilds its catalogue copy from the replay
a fresh instance rebuilds its catalogue copy from the replay
a fresh instance rebuilds its catalogue copy from the replay

rows.title: Replay every site's schedule at start-up
rows.story: In the same start-up pass, the current cut-off schedule of each site is announced again, in full, for the same reason: a fresh consumer must be able to rebuild its copy.
rows.policy: Whenever the service starts, announce every site's schedule again

then.does: a fresh instance rebuilds its cut-off copy from the replay
a fresh instance rebuilds its cut-off copy from the replay

rows.title: Count catalogue growth for reports
rows.story: The service reads its own path announcements and keeps a daily tally of paths defined, revised and retired, which feeds the catalogue growth report. It never reads another context's events.
rows.policy: Whenever a path is created, revised or retired, add one to that day's tally

hotspots.text: The site id of a cut-off schedule is never checked. A schedule for an unknown site only shows up later as an unroutable order in order-management.
ICQA (inventory control) is deliberately left undecided: it may become a path family, stay in inventory-storage, or call into it.
wes-work-planning and network-inventory-planning do not yet filter on the declared intake values; they route by explicit path id.
How long announcements are kept is not set here. Consumers rebuild their copy by replaying them all, so the start-up replay is the safety net.

opportunities.text: Log compaction would let the broker keep only the latest announcement per path and per site. It is a warehouse-infra change.
If the fleet gets a real transportation context, the cut-off schedule can move there unchanged. Its place here is provisional.

product-content.oneLine: Holds the description, media and category of each catalogue item, publishes it when complete, and retires it when the item is discontinued.

rows.title: Start the content of an item
rows.story: A content manager creates a draft for a catalogue item the network already knows. Items the network has discontinued are refused. A draft may be incomplete, and nothing is published yet.

rows.title: Revise the content
rows.story: The content manager replaces the description, bullets, attributes and media. A draft or live content takes a new revision. Shoppers see it only after the next publish. Retired content cannot be revised.

rows.title: Discard a draft
rows.story: The content manager throws away a draft that was never published. It is retired as discarded, and nothing is announced because the shopper never saw it.

rows.title: Publish the content
rows.story: The content manager publishes. It needs a description, exactly one main media item and a category in the tree, and a known, live item. The full content leaves with its revision. Publishing a revision already live does nothing.

then.does: replaces the item's content in its product view, only if the revision is newer

rows.title: Withdraw published content
rows.story: The content manager takes published content down by hand. Retired content is final: it can never be changed or published again.

then.does: ends the item's published content in its product view

rows.title: Add a category
rows.story: The content manager adds a category, at the top or under a parent. The tree has at most four levels and sibling names are unique. There is no draft tree: every change publishes a new version of the whole tree.

then.does: replaces its category view when the tree version is newer

rows.title: Move a category
rows.story: The content manager moves a category, with its sub-categories, under another parent. A move into its own subtree, or past four levels, is refused. The new tree version is published.

then.does: replaces its category view when the tree version is newer

rows.title: Rename a category
rows.story: The content manager renames a category. The paths of its sub-categories follow, and sibling names stay unique. The new tree version is published.

then.does: replaces its category view when the tree version is newer

rows.title: Send the category tree again
rows.story: The content manager republishes the tree without changing it, so a consumer can catch up. It goes out under the next version.

then.does: replaces its category view when the tree version is newer

rows.title: Keep the list of catalogue items
rows.story: offer-availability announces each new item. This context keeps a copy, so it can refuse content for an unknown item without asking. A discontinued item is never made active again by a late message.
rows.policy: Whenever an item is created, record it as active unless it is already known

rows.title: Retire content when an item is discontinued
rows.story: The network discontinues an item. Published content is retired and announced. A draft is retired quietly, since nothing was ever published. A discontinued item can no longer be published.
rows.policy: Whenever an item is discontinued, mark it so and retire its published and draft content

then.does: ends the item's published content in its product view

hotspots.text: Media are plain links to static files. Nothing fetches or checks them, so a broken link can be published.
Content for an item not yet announced is refused, not queued. A quick write can fail only because this copy lags.
Published content stays up until the discontinue notice arrives. The design assumes it will eventually.
Categories can never be deleted. The 'category in use' refusal exists for a future removal and nothing raises it.
Every category change republishes the whole tree, even a move to the same parent or a rename to the same name.

opportunities.text: Promotions, reviews and recommendations are left for later phases.

product-discovery.oneLine: The shopper-facing read side: keeps searchable product pages and a category tree up to date from other contexts' events, and works out what is purchasable.

rows.title: Add a new item to the catalogue view
rows.story: offer-availability announces a new catalogue item. The product row gets its title and flags and becomes visible. If a price or listing arrived first, a hidden placeholder row is completed.
rows.policy: Whenever a catalogue item is created, complete its product row and mark it active

rows.title: Show the published content
rows.story: product-content publishes the description, bullets, attributes, media and main category of a product. Only a newer revision replaces what is shown, and the product becomes searchable.
rows.policy: Whenever content is published, replace the product's content if its revision is newer

rows.title: Keep the category tree
rows.story: product-content publishes the whole category tree. A newer version replaces the old one and the purchasable counts per category are worked out again. No product row has to change.
rows.policy: Whenever a category tree is published, replace the current one if its version is newer

rows.title: Show the current price
rows.story: pricing announces a new list and sale price. A newer version replaces the prices on the product and makes the price count towards being purchasable.
rows.policy: Whenever a price changes, store the new prices if the version is newer

rows.title: Add a listing to a product
rows.story: offer-availability says a node now offers the item. The product gets a live listing with no stock yet, and the view learns which item the listing belongs to.
rows.policy: Whenever a listing is created, add it to its product and remember which item it belongs to

rows.title: Update the stock of a product
rows.story: offer-availability reports how many units a listing can ship. A newer report replaces the old count, and the product shows in stock if any live listing has units.
rows.policy: Whenever a quantity is reported, store it if it is newer and recheck in stock and purchasable

rows.title: Hide a suppressed listing
rows.story: A suppressed listing stops counting as stock. The event names only the listing, so the item is found in the listing-to-item map. An unknown listing is skipped with a warning.
rows.policy: Whenever a listing is suppressed, mark it suppressed so it no longer counts as stock

rows.title: Bring a restored listing back
rows.story: A restored listing counts as stock again, found through the listing-to-item map like a suppression. An unknown listing is skipped with a warning.
rows.policy: Whenever a listing is restored, mark it live so its units count as stock again

rows.title: Retire a product's content
rows.story: product-content ends a product's published content. The row stays, but it is no longer searchable or purchasable. A later, higher revision can publish it again.
rows.policy: Whenever content is retired, mark it retired unless an older revision is being retired

rows.title: Withdraw a price from a product
rows.story: pricing withdraws an item's price. The amounts are cleared and the product is no longer purchasable, even if it is in stock.
rows.policy: Whenever a price is withdrawn, clear the amounts unless a newer price was already stored

rows.title: Mark a discontinued item
rows.story: The item is marked discontinued and is never purchasable again. Its page stays and reads as currently unavailable. A late creation event cannot bring it back.
rows.policy: Whenever an item is discontinued, mark its row discontinued

rows.title: Rebuild the views from scratch
rows.story: An operator runs a one-off job that reads every source page by page and refills the product and category views with the same rules as live events. Events that follow are not applied twice.

hotspots.text: A silent producer or a stalled consumer leaves the views stale. There is no freshness metric and no alert on lag.
The list of handled events and the messages parked after failing grow without bound. No pruning job exists.
A suppress or restore that arrives before its listing is known is skipped with a warning. Only a rebuild repairs it.
A producer that resets its version or revision counter has its new facts ignored as stale.

opportunities.text: Search runs on the database today; a dedicated search engine can sit behind the same port later.
Recommendations, reviews, personalisation and sponsored placement are later phases; ranking weights are fixed today.

product-master.oneLine: Owns what a SKU is: its description, handling class, unit size and pack levels with their barcodes (GTINs). Other contexts keep copies.

rows.title: Register a product
rows.story: A steward registers a new SKU. Nothing else can be said about a SKU until it exists: classifying or sizing an unknown SKU is refused, never an implicit registration.

then.does: adds the SKU to its known SKUs, so an ASN line for it is accepted

rows.title: Change a product's description
rows.story: The steward sends new text for a SKU that already exists. The same text again changes nothing and raises no event.

rows.title: Classify a product for handling
rows.story: The steward sets the handling tags (such as hazmat or fragile), the temperature class and the hazard class. A later classification replaces the earlier one. Other contexts keep their own copy.

then.does: keeps a copy for stow-time placement and segregation checks
keeps a copy to enrich incoming orders
keeps a copy for the capabilities and the fragile flag at release
keeps a copy for segregation checks when sealing a package
keeps tags and temperature class to match SKUs to slots
keeps a copy of each SKU's handling class

rows.title: Declare a unit's size and weight
rows.story: The steward states the length, width, height and weight of one unit, as the vendor or catalogue says. Values outside the allowed range are refused.

then.does: refreshes the unit size it uses to fit SKUs into slots

rows.title: Record a measured unit
rows.story: A dimensioning device or a person reports what one real unit measures. The latest reading wins and an older one is refused. More than 10 % off the declared size is flagged, not rejected.

then.does: uses the measured size in place of the declared one

rows.title: Declare a pack level and its GTIN
rows.story: The steward declares a pack level (each, inner, case or pallet) with its barcode and how many units it holds. A barcode can identify only one SKU and level, fleet-wide and for ever.

then.does: keeps a packaging view so a scanned barcode resolves to a SKU and a unit count
keeps its own packaging view of levels and GTINs
keeps pack sizes to plan case-pick faces
keeps the pack levels for scan checks
keeps a copy of the pack levels
keeps a pack-level view

rows.title: Switch a level to a new GTIN
rows.story: Declaring a different barcode at a level that is already active retires the old one as superseded and declares the new one, in one step. The old GTIN stays resolvable for ASNs still in flight.

then.does: ends the old GTIN in its packaging view and adds the new one
ends the old GTIN in its packaging view and adds the new one

rows.title: Retire a pack level
rows.story: The steward ends a pack level. The level and its GTIN are kept for look-ups. Retiring a level that is already retired changes nothing.

then.does: plans a SKU whose case level is retired on an each-pick face
ends the level in its copy of the pack levels

rows.title: Record a measured pack
rows.story: A device or operator measures one pack of an active level, such as a case. Like a unit reading, an older one is refused, and a weight below the contents is refused.

then.does: keeps the measured size with its copy of the pack level

rows.title: Feed the data quality report
rows.story: Each unit event is also written to a separate stream. A reporting service folds it into a data quality view: how many SKUs are registered, classified, sized and measured.
rows.policy: Whenever a product event is published, add it to the data quality report's own copy

hotspots.text: A SKU classified moments before its first stow may reach a consumer late. Consumers keep their own rules for an unknown SKU.
The size tolerance is fixed at 10 %, and only the latest measurement is kept, with no history of readings.
A classification can be replaced but never removed: there is no unclassify command or event.
Weighed, variable-measure items are refused: a GTIN with indicator digit 9 is rejected in v1.
After the publisher gives up on a stuck message, later ones overtake it, even for the same SKU. Consumers rely on the version to cope.

opportunities.text: Expected package weight at the weigh check, slot fit at stow and cube-based capacity could use the effective unit size. None is built.
A per-category size tolerance instead of the fixed 10 % is named as a later decision.

returns-processing.oneLine: Handles returned goods: authorizes a return for a shipped line, receives and grades the parcel, decides its fate and hands restockable units to stock.

rows.title: Keep the product classes
rows.story: product-master classifies each product (for example hazmat or temperature class). Returns keeps the latest version as a local copy, so grading never needs a live call.
rows.policy: Whenever a product is classified, keep it if its version is newer than the copy

rows.title: Keep the allocated order lines
rows.story: order-management announces which order lines were allocated and with which product. Returns keeps them, so a return request never has to name the product itself.
rows.policy: Whenever order lines are allocated, store each line with its product

rows.title: Keep the manifested packages
rows.story: fulfillment-execution reports each manifested package. A line with a manifested package is proof that it shipped, which a return needs.
rows.policy: Whenever a package is manifested, record which order line it carried

rows.title: Set the return rules
rows.story: An operator declares a version of the disposition policy: return window, unit cap per line and which outcome each grade and product class gets. The newest version becomes current.

rows.title: Authorize a return
rows.story: An operator asks to take back units of a shipped order line. It is authorized only if the line shipped, the window is open, no other return is open for it and the quantity is within the cap.

rows.title: Refuse a return request (event not raised yet)
rows.story: A refused request is answered with an error and nothing is saved or published. The refusal event and the reject step exist in the domain, but no use case raises them yet.

rows.title: Open a receipt for the arrived parcel
rows.story: A parcel arrives. Every line is either matched to a return authorization or recorded as unexpected, never silently accepted.

then.does: opens a case for each unexpected line

rows.title: Grade a returned line
rows.story: An inspector grades one received line A, B, C or SCRAP, with reason codes. Each line is graded exactly once, for no more units than were received.

rows.title: Decide what happens to the line
rows.story: In the same step as the grading, the rules turn grade, product class and current policy into an outcome. A RESTOCK below grade B, or of hazmat with no hazard rating, is swapped for the policy's fallback outcome.
rows.policy: Whenever a line is graded, decide its outcome from the grade, product class and policy

rows.title: Hand restockable units to stock
rows.story: When the outcome is RESTOCK, the line is staged exactly once so the warehouse stock can take the units back. No other outcome touches another context.
rows.policy: Whenever the outcome is RESTOCK, stage the line once for inventory-storage

then.does: books the returned units as staged stock

rows.title: Override a decision
rows.story: An operator replaces an outcome and must give a reason. The original is kept; a new decision points back to it. An override to RESTOCK stages the line like any other.

then.does: books the returned units as staged stock

hotspots.text: The shipped quantity is unknown: allocated lines carry no quantity, so a return is capped by the policy only.
The refusal event is declared but no use case raises it. A refused request answers with an error and leaves no trace.
A staged line's stow is invisible here, so nothing shows that restocked units reached a bin.
No use case moves a return authorization past AUTHORIZED. The receipt alone carries the arrival.

opportunities.text: A shipped-quantity check per line is planned once order-management adds a quantity to its allocated lines.
Consuming the stowed-item fact from inventory-storage could close the loop from a staged line to a bin.

seller-inbound.oneLine: Lets a seller plan, pack, label and ship stock to a network node, checks what actually arrives, and advises where to send more.

rows.title: Onboard a seller
rows.story: A network partner manager registers a seller. The seller starts active and can plan inbound shipments straight away. Onboarding an existing seller id is refused.

rows.title: Plan an inbound shipment
rows.story: A seller says what it will send: a node, a packing style (loose or case-packed) and up to 500 item lines in single units. The node must be able to receive. The draft is private to the seller, so nothing is announced.

rows.title: Confirm the plan
rows.story: The seller confirms the draft. The seller must still be active and the node still able to receive. A confirmed plan can be filled by several shipments.

rows.title: Pack a carton
rows.story: The seller adds a carton to a draft shipment. A carton without an SSCC (the standard carton id) gets one issued. It must fit the node's weight and size limits and the plan, and a case carton must match a declared case size.

rows.title: Label the shipment
rows.story: The seller seals the shipment. Contents are frozen and the whole carton list is announced, so the vendor knows what to expect. For a plan with a single shipment the cartons must match every plan line.

then.does: keeps the carton list in the inbound shipment view it serves to vendors

rows.title: Ship the shipment
rows.story: The seller sends the labelled shipment. It then waits for the vendor's receipt. The seller must still be active and the node still able to receive.

then.does: marks the shipment as shipped in the view it serves to vendors
keeps the shipped time, to measure how long the delivery takes

rows.title: Check what the vendor received
rows.story: The vendor reports carton by carton what it found. The first answer per carton is final. Missing, unexpected or damaged cartons and short or over counts are recorded, and each compliance code raised is recorded as a violation.
rows.policy: Whenever a vendor submits a receipt, apply it carton by carton and record every difference

rows.title: Close the shipment
rows.story: Once every carton on the list has an answer the shipment closes, as clean or with discrepancies. The closing fact lists the stock that really arrived, per item.
rows.policy: Whenever the last carton gets an answer, close the shipment and announce what arrived

then.does: creates the seller's own listings from the stock that arrived
marks the shipment as received in the view it serves to vendors

rows.title: Suspend a seller
rows.story: A network partner manager suspends a seller. A suspended seller can plan, pack and ship nothing; a shipment already on its way still closes on the vendor's receipt. Suspending twice does nothing.

then.does: suppresses the seller's listings

rows.title: Reinstate a seller
rows.story: A network partner manager lifts a suspension. The seller can plan and ship again. Reinstating an active seller does nothing.

then.does: restores the seller's listings

rows.title: Advise where to send more stock
rows.story: A seller asks where more of one item should go. The advice covers each region with demand in the last 28 days and splits the shortfall over its fulfilment centres. No demand gives an empty plan. A new plan replaces the old one.

rows.title: Accept the advice
rows.story: The seller accepts a suggested plan. It is only recorded: nothing downstream changes, and the seller still ships through the normal plan flow.

rows.title: Keep the list of nodes that can receive
rows.story: node-topology announces nodes, their inbound limits and their status. This context keeps a copy, so it never asks live. A node it has not seen as active cannot receive.
rows.policy: Whenever a node is registered, declared, activated, suspended or retired, update its row

rows.title: Keep the packaging levels
rows.story: offer-availability announces each item's pack levels: each, case, pallet. Case cartons are checked against them, so the sizes must be known before a case carton can be packed.
rows.policy: Whenever a pack level is declared or retired, update the packaging levels

rows.title: Keep the stock each node declares
rows.story: offer-availability says how much of an item each node lists. The advice splits a shortfall by this stock.
rows.policy: Whenever a listing's availability changes, keep the latest figure per item and node

rows.title: Keep the regional demand (not switched on)
rows.story: order-sourcing says where order lines were sent. The advice sums them per region. The code exists, but the running service does not start this consumer, so the demand copy stays empty.
rows.policy: Whenever an order is released to a node, keep its lines as demand for that region

hotspots.text: The demand half of the placement advice is never filled: the order-sourcing consumer exists but is not started, so advice comes out empty.
A shipped shipment that is never received has no timeout. It stays shipped until a receipt arrives.
Compliance violations are recorded and nothing acts on them. The scorecard is informational and never suspends a seller.
Plan lines are not checked against whether the item is still live, because discontinued items are not followed.
Accepting placement advice drives nothing downstream. The seller ships by hand through the normal plan flow.

opportunities.text: Placement optimisation can follow in a later decision, once the advice has consumers.
A minimum number of receipts before a seller's tier counts, if a machine ever reads the tier.

shipping-and-tracking.oneLine: Issues shipping labels and keeps one timeline per package, from handover to delivery, return or loss.

rows.title: Issue a label for a package
rows.story: A vendor asks for a label for one package of a purchase order. The shipping address is fetched live and checked; if it looks like a placeholder the label is refused. Otherwise the label and the package's journey start together.

then.does: adds the tracking number to the booking's expected volume
creates the package row that the order's tracking view reads
keeps the opaque stop id and postal prefix so it can group packages into stops

rows.title: Void a label
rows.story: An operator voids a label that should not be used. It only works while the package is still waiting for pickup; once it is handed over the void is refused.

then.does: marks the package as voided
drops the tracking number from the expected volume; the booking stays

rows.title: Record a scan by hand
rows.story: An operator adds a scan to a package's journey. It follows the same rules as scans from partners: an old, repeated or impossible scan is refused, and a handover or delivery scan also announces that milestone.

then.does: adds the scan to the order's tracking timeline
judges a handover against the purchase order's ship-by date
records a delivery and judges the promise when it was the last package
records a delivered package; the last one delivers the assignment

rows.title: Note the vendor's shipment confirmation
rows.story: The vendor says a shipment has left. Each package on it gets a 'shipment confirmed' scan, but its journey does not move: the handover waits for the carrier's pickup.
rows.policy: Whenever a vendor confirms a shipment, add one scan per tracking number

then.does: adds the scan to the order's tracking timeline

rows.title: Hand the package over at pickup
rows.story: A load leaves its origin. The first pickup departure of a labelled package hands it over to the carrier; any later departure is just a movement.
rows.policy: Whenever a load departs, add one scan per package; the first pickup hands it over

then.does: judges the handover against the purchase order's ship-by date
adds the scan to the order's tracking timeline

rows.title: Follow the package through the middle mile
rows.story: A load arrives. At a delivery station the package becomes ready to go out; at any other hub it stays in transit.
rows.policy: Whenever a load arrives, add one scan per package: station arrival or transit arrival

then.does: adds the scan to the order's tracking timeline

rows.title: Show the package out for delivery
rows.story: The delivery station sends the package out on a route. The journey moves to out for delivery.
rows.policy: Whenever a package goes out for delivery, add an out-for-delivery scan

then.does: adds the scan to the order's tracking timeline

rows.title: Close the journey on delivery
rows.story: A delivery attempt ends. A successful one delivers the package and closes the journey; a failed one sends it back to the station and the journey stays open.
rows.policy: Whenever an attempt is made, add a delivered or failed scan to the journey

then.does: records the delivery and judges the promise when it was the last package
records a delivered package; the last one delivers the assignment
marks the package and its order group delivered

rows.title: Return a package to the sender
rows.story: After repeated failed attempts, last-mile-delivery starts a return. A package waiting at the station becomes returned, which ends its journey.
rows.policy: Whenever a return is started, mark the package at the station as returned

then.does: records the return and judges the promise broken
marks the package and its order group returned
refunds the order, or waits until its payment exists

rows.title: Store the day-of delivery window
rows.story: When a route starts, last-mile-delivery gives each stop a time window. Every package of the stop keeps it; the window shows only while the package is out for delivery.
rows.policy: Whenever a stop gets a time window, store it on each package of the stop

then.does: keeps the window for the order's tracking view unless a newer one exists

rows.title: Relay a delivery-point warning
rows.story: last-mile-delivery flags a delivery point after two failed attempts. It knows the stop, not the order, so this context passes the warning on for each package of the stop, without any address.
rows.policy: Whenever a delivery point is flagged, store the flag on each open package of the stop

then.does: keeps the flag on the package's tracking view so the shopper can be advised

rows.title: Raise an exception on silence
rows.story: A periodic sweep looks for open packages with no new scan for longer than their service tier allows. Each silent package gets one exception until a new scan arrives.
rows.policy: Every sweep, any package silent past its window raises one exception

then.does: treats the exception as a risk to the promise and may re-promise
records the exception on the order's tracking view

rows.title: Declare a silent package lost
rows.story: If a package in transit stays silent for 48 hours after its exception, the same sweep declares it lost and closes its journey.
rows.policy: Every sweep, an in-transit package with an unanswered exception for 48 hours is lost

then.does: records the loss and judges the promise broken
marks the package and its order group lost
refunds the order, or waits until its payment exists

rows.title: Keep the product dimensions copy
rows.story: Every product that offer-availability creates leaves its size, weight and handling flags here. Nothing reads them yet.
rows.policy: Whenever a catalogue item is created, store its dimensions and handling flags

rows.title: Delete old delivery addresses
rows.story: The saved, encrypted delivery address is deleted 30 days after its journey closes, whether delivered, returned, lost or voided.
rows.policy: Every housekeeping run, delete addresses of journeys closed over 30 days ago

hotspots.text: Voiding a label and recording a scan by hand have no named caller: the routes are unauthenticated and the contracts name nobody.
A placeholder-looking address refuses the label, but no loop asks the shopper to fix it. That is deliberately left out.
News about a package this context never labelled is counted and dropped. Nothing keeps it for a later look.
A delivery-point warning is never cleared by an event. It ends only when the package's journey ends.
A restricted route through which partners could resolve the delivery address is not built.

opportunities.text: The product dimensions copy has no reader yet. It is kept so a printable label can use it later.

shopping-cart.oneLine: Holds a shopper's cart before checkout: lines, destination, chosen delivery offers and a non-binding estimate. Closes the cart once checkout completes.

rows.title: Start a cart
rows.story: A shopper, signed in or not, opens an empty cart. Nothing is announced to other contexts.

rows.title: Add an item to the cart
rows.story: The shopper adds an item. It must be known, priced and not discontinued. Adding an item already in the cart merges the quantities, which must stay between 1 and 99.

rows.title: Change a quantity
rows.story: The shopper sets a new quantity for a line. Any change to the lines throws away the delivery offers and selections, so they have to be asked for again.

rows.title: Remove an item
rows.story: The shopper removes a line. Like any change to the lines, it clears the delivery offers and selections. Nothing is announced.

rows.title: Say where it should be delivered
rows.story: The shopper gives a destination postal prefix. Until then the estimate shows only the item total; delivery and tax appear once a destination is set.

rows.title: Get delivery offers
rows.story: The cart asks delivery-promise for delivery offers for its lines and destination, and keeps them. Offers hold no capacity, they are facts frozen at quote time.

rows.title: Choose a delivery offer
rows.story: The shopper picks one offer for each shipment group. An offer that is not part of the current quote is refused. The cart is ready for checkout when every group has an offer and none has expired.

rows.title: Merge a guest cart after sign-in
rows.story: When a guest signs in, the guest cart's lines move into the shopper's open cart and the guest cart is closed as merged. Quantities add up, capped at 99.

rows.title: Take over the offers of a checkout requote
rows.story: When checkout finds that the offers have to be requoted, it can write the new ones into the cart. They replace the quote and are selected for every group, with no call to delivery-promise.

rows.title: Keep the item list
