rows.story: offer-availability announces new and discontinued catalogue items. The cart keeps a copy of which items exist and which are discontinued, so adding an item needs no live call.
rows.policy: Whenever an item is created or discontinued, update what the cart knows of it

rows.title: Keep the item prices
rows.story: pricing announces each item's current price, and withdraws it when an item can no longer be sold. The cart keeps the newest price, and an item without a price cannot be added.
rows.policy: Whenever a price changes or is withdrawn, keep it if its version is newer

rows.title: Keep the delivery charges
rows.story: pricing publishes the charge for each delivery speed. The cart replaces its copy and uses it to estimate the delivery cost. Only the estimate moves; the cart's own delivery offers are left alone.
rows.policy: Whenever a charge schedule is published, replace the stored one if it is newer

rows.title: Keep the tax rates
rows.story: pricing publishes the tax rates by destination postal prefix. The cart replaces its copy and uses it for the estimate, which is labelled non-binding.
rows.policy: Whenever a tax table is published, replace the stored one if it is newer

rows.title: Close the cart when checkout completes
rows.story: checkout reports that the purchase went through. The open cart is closed as checked out. A cart that is unknown or not open only gets a warning in the log.
rows.policy: Whenever a checkout completes, close the cart as checked out

rows.title: Abandon carts nobody touches
rows.story: A sweep closes every open cart that has not changed for 30 days as abandoned and announces it.
rows.policy: Every sweep, an open cart unchanged for 30 days is abandoned

rows.title: Delete old closed carts
rows.story: A second sweep deletes carts that are no longer open and have not changed for 30 days. Nothing is announced, so an idle cart is gone about 60 days after its last change.
rows.policy: Every sweep, a closed cart unchanged for 30 days is deleted

hotspots.text: Only adding a line, quoting, abandoning and checking out publish an event. Removals, quantity changes, destinations, selections and merges raise nothing.
The cart accepts any known, priced, undiscontinued item without checking stock. It is lenient on purpose: checkout's binding price quote is the gate.
No context reads the cart's events. Whether a sibling should ever consume one is undecided.
The route that lets checkout write a requote into the cart has no caller yet in the local checkouts.

opportunities.text: Promotions inside the estimate are a later phase and would add complexity to the cart.
A deferred identity context would take over the guest-first shopper ids and the cart merge the cart handles today.

slotting-optimization.oneLine: Proposes which SKU belongs in which forward pick slot, from recent demand. A planner reviews each plan; only an approved plan changes the map.

rows.title: Draft a slot plan
rows.story: A planner asks for a plan. SKUs are ranked by recent picks, and each gets the best slot it fits. The plan lists the moves and the SKUs it could not place. Nothing on the floor changes yet.
rows.policy: Rank SKUs by picks, keep a SKU in its slot when still eligible, give the rest the best free slot

rows.title: Approve a plan
rows.story: The planner approves a Draft plan. The site's earlier approved plan is replaced in the same step, so each site has one. The event carries the whole map and every move, so nobody has to ask back.

then.does: plans one relocation job for each move of the plan
updates its own view of the forward faces
replaces its map of which SKU sits on which forward face

rows.title: Reject a plan
rows.story: The planner turns a Draft plan down, with an optional reason. The forward-slot map stays as it was.

rows.title: Keep the demand copy
rows.story: order-management reports what each site's order lines demand. The latest report for a line wins, and a removed line stays on file as inactive.
rows.policy: Whenever demand for a line changes, store the latest state of that line

rows.title: Keep the handling class copy
rows.story: product-master classifies SKUs. Slotting keeps the handling tags and temperature class, so hazmat and cold goods only go to slots that suit them.
rows.policy: Whenever a product is classified, keep the copy only if the version is newer

rows.title: Keep the unit size copy
rows.story: product-master reports a unit's declared or measured size. Slotting keeps the size in use, because a SKU without a size cannot be placed and is listed as unassigned.
rows.policy: Whenever a unit size is declared or measured, keep the effective size if the version is newer

rows.title: Keep the pack level copy
rows.story: A SKU is planned onto a case-pick face only if it has an active case level with a size. Slotting keeps the declared, retired and measured pack levels, so it never asks product-master.
rows.policy: Whenever a pack level is declared, retired or measured, keep the newer version

rows.title: Keep the zone list
rows.story: facility-layout announces each zone with its temperature class and hazmat flag. Slotting keeps them to know which zones are forward zones and what they can hold.
rows.policy: Whenever a zone is registered, store or refresh it

rows.title: Keep the slot list
rows.story: facility-layout announces every location slot with its weight and volume limits. Slotting keeps them, and a slot that was decommissioned is never brought back by a late message.
rows.policy: Whenever a slot is registered, store or refresh it, unless it is already decommissioned

rows.title: Drop a decommissioned slot
rows.story: When a slot is decommissioned it stops being a candidate for good, even if slotting never saw it registered.
rows.policy: Whenever a slot is decommissioned, mark it inactive for good

rows.title: Track how far a plan is executed
rows.story: inventory-storage reports each stock relocation. When it matches a move of an approved plan, slotting records the move as done, once per relocation. The plan then shows moves done out of total.
rows.policy: Whenever stock is relocated for slotting, record the matching plan move as executed

rows.title: Feed the plan funnel report
rows.story: Every plan event is also written to a separate stream. A reporting service counts plans generated, approved and rejected per day, and how long approval took.
rows.policy: Whenever a plan decision is published, add it to the funnel report's own copy

hotspots.text: Slots are ranked by location code, not travel distance, because layout events carry none. "Best" slot means "first code".
Never checked on live data: that the forward zone code is FWD and that a demand site id equals a facility site code. If not, plans come out short.
Execution progress is advisory. A newer plan can be approved while the previous one is half executed.
A better-ranked SKU can take another SKU's slot and set off a chain of relocations. Accepted for v1 and visible in the moves.

opportunities.text: Holding new proposals until the previous plan is executed would need a new decision. Not built.
Replenishment min/max, shared slots, reserve-zone slotting and automatic approval are all named as later decisions.

task-interleaving.oneLine: After a station finishes a task, suggests the few nearest open tasks so operators walk less between jobs. Advice only: it never assigns or claims work.

rows.title: Set a site's hint rules
rows.story: An operator sets, for one site, how far a detour may be, how many suggestions to give, how long a hint lives and which task types qualify. Until a site has rules it gets no hints at all.

rows.title: Suggest the next tasks after a completion
rows.story: A station finishes a task, so it now stands at that task's end point. If the site has rules, the nearest open tasks are ranked and issued as a hint. A new hint replaces the station's older live one.
rows.policy: Whenever a task is completed, record where the station stands and, if the site has rules, rank the nearest open tasks

then.does: keeps the hint and uses it to break a tie within one priority band when the station claims its next task

rows.title: Notice that a hint was followed
rows.story: A station claims a task. The task leaves the open list. If it was one of the live hint's suggestions and the hint had not run out, the hint counts as taken. Claiming any other task changes nothing.
rows.policy: Whenever a task is claimed, take it off the open list and mark the station's live hint taken if it named that task

rows.title: Let an unused hint expire
rows.story: A hint lives only for the time the site's rules allow. A frequent sweep marks every live hint past its deadline as expired, even when the station does nothing.
rows.policy: Every few seconds, any live hint past its deadline is marked expired

rows.title: Preview the advice for a station
rows.story: Anyone can ask what the recommender would suggest for a station, from its last known position or from a location they name. It changes nothing and sends nothing.

rows.title: Keep the open-task list
rows.story: fulfillment-execution announces every task that becomes claimable. This context keeps its own copy of that pool, so it can rank tasks without asking. A task already completed never returns to it.
rows.policy: Whenever a task becomes claimable, add it to the open tasks with its type, site and locations

rows.title: Keep the zone list
rows.story: facility-layout announces each zone of a site. Here the zone list links every location to its site, so a task's location can be placed on the right map.
rows.policy: Whenever a zone is registered, add it to the zone list with its site

rows.title: Keep the location list
rows.story: Each new storage location announced by facility-layout is added to the local list with its zone. Distances can only be measured between places listed here.
rows.policy: Whenever a location slot is registered, add it to the location list with its zone

rows.title: Retire a location
rows.story: When facility-layout takes a location out of service, it is retired in the local list for good.
rows.policy: Whenever a location slot is decommissioned, retire it in the location list

rows.title: Keep the location points
rows.story: facility-layout reports where a location sits on the floor, in metres. These points are what the distance between two places is measured from. A place with no point is skipped, never guessed.
rows.policy: Whenever a location's position changes, store its new point, even if the location is not listed yet

rows.title: Measure how much advice is followed
rows.story: The service reads its own hint announcements and keeps a daily tally of hints issued, taken and expired. That tally feeds the hint adoption report.
rows.policy: Whenever a hint is issued, taken or expires, add it to that day's tally

hotspots.text: A completion with no candidate leaves an older live hint in place until it expires. Retracting it would need a new event.
PACK, SLAM and REBIN tasks have no location in fulfillment-execution, so they are never announced and can never be hinted.
It is assumed that fulfillment's site ids equal facility-layout's site codes and that one map frame covers a site. Not yet checked on live data.
A place with no known point is skipped, never guessed. Sparse map data means short hint lists or none at all.

opportunities.text: A travel model aware of aisles, cross-aisles and fixed structures is a planned refinement of today's straight-line distance.
Multi-stop batching, cross-station balancing and hints on the station screen are named as later decisions.

vendor-connectivity.oneLine: The network's front door for vendors: issues purchase orders to vendor-run nodes and takes their answers, labels, shipments, stock feeds and inbound receipts.

rows.title: Onboard a vendor
rows.story: A partner manager creates a vendor account and sets how long the vendor has to acknowledge each purchase order. Onboarding the same vendor again returns the existing account.

rows.title: Suspend a vendor
rows.story: A partner manager suspends a vendor. While suspended, every write the vendor sends is refused.

rows.title: Reinstate a vendor
rows.story: A partner manager lifts the suspension and the vendor can write again.

rows.title: Issue a purchase order
rows.story: When a group is released to a vendor-run node, one purchase order is issued to that node's vendor. It names the stock owner of every line and the time by which the vendor must answer.
rows.policy: Whenever a group is released to a vendor-run node, issue one purchase order for it

then.does: tracks the order for the node's scorecard

rows.title: Acknowledge a purchase order
rows.story: The vendor's system polls its orders, then accepts or rejects the whole order in one call. It must cover every line and answer before the deadline. The call returns a transaction id, not the result.

rows.title: Settle the vendor's queued writes
rows.story: A processor runs each queued vendor write once it is due and records the outcome. A successful acknowledgement becomes an accepted or rejected order, a successful shipment confirmation a shipped one.
rows.policy: Whenever a queued vendor write is due, run it and apply its outcome to the purchase order

then.does: locks the group on acceptance, tries another node on rejection, marks it shipped
records a shipment-confirmed scan for each tracking number
counts the answer and the shipment for the node's scorecard

rows.title: Expire an order nobody answered
rows.story: A sweep finds issued orders past their acknowledge-by time. They expire so order-sourcing can try another node.
rows.policy: Every sweep, an issued order past its acknowledge-by time expires

then.does: excludes the node and searches again
counts the missed deadline for the node's scorecard

rows.title: Cancel an order when sourcing cancels
rows.story: When order-sourcing cancels a group, its purchase order is cancelled, but only while it still waits for the vendor's answer. After the vendor answered, the order stays and the refusal is only logged.
rows.policy: Whenever a group is cancelled, cancel its purchase order if it is still waiting for an answer

rows.title: Cancel an order when a release is withdrawn
rows.story: When order-sourcing withdraws a merged release, the purchase order of exactly that release is cancelled, never a newer one for the same group.
rows.policy: Whenever a release is withdrawn, cancel the purchase order of that release if it is still waiting

rows.title: Request shipping labels
rows.story: For an accepted order the vendor asks for one label per package. This is the one write answered at once: one label is issued per package by shipping-and-tracking, and labels already issued are returned again.

then.does: is called right away to issue one label per package

rows.title: Confirm a shipment
rows.story: The vendor confirms that an accepted order shipped. The tracking numbers must be exactly the ones of the labels issued; the confirmation is queued and settled later.

rows.title: Register a node or send its stock
rows.story: The vendor registers a node, declares its operating profile or sends an inventory feed. Each write is queued and settled later; node-topology and offer-availability do the real work and the answer carries the new node id.

rows.title: Report what the dock received
rows.story: The vendor reports cartons received for an inbound shipment. The report is checked against the shipment's manifest; counting more or fewer units than listed is reported, never refused.

then.does: records the findings and closes the inbound shipment
uses the carton findings for the node's inbound accuracy score

rows.title: Keep the inbound shipments copy
rows.story: Seller-inbound announces shipments with their carton manifests. A copy lets the vendor poll what is on its way and lets receipts be checked without a live call.
rows.policy: Whenever an inbound shipment is labelled, shipped or received, update the local shipments copy

rows.title: Keep the vendor node list
rows.story: Node-topology announces nodes, profiles and status changes. A copy tells which nodes belong to which vendor and each node's handling time, used to set the answer deadline.
rows.policy: Whenever a node is registered, profiled, activated, suspended or retired, update the local node list

rows.title: Keep the listings and packaging copy
rows.story: Offer-availability announces listings and the pack levels of each catalogue item. Listings let stock feeds be checked; pack levels appear on purchase order lines.
rows.policy: Whenever a listing is created, keep it so a stock feed can be checked against its node

hotspots.text: A cancel that arrives after the vendor answered is refused and only logged: nobody is told, and the vendor may still ship.
The vendor's identity is a request field, not authentication. The ownership check only keeps a vendor away from other vendors' nodes inside the cluster.
A withdrawn release can be accepted in the one message hop before the cancel arrives: the vendor then holds an order for the old merged lines.
A receipt is judged when it is sent, not again when processed, so two receipts for one shipment can both be accepted.
The vendor-account events (onboarded, suspended, reinstated) have no consumer that acts on them yet.

warehouse-planning.oneLine: Answers 'can this site handle the demand in this time window?': it works out how much a process path can do, plans against demand and announces any shortage.

rows.title: Declare how fast one station works
rows.story: An operator states how much one station of a process handles per hour at a site. The station counts from the floor map are multiplied by this figure when a path's capacity is worked out.

rows.title: Declare the labour a dock booking costs
rows.story: An operator states how many labour minutes a dock appointment, and each shipment notice on it, costs at a site for a process path. Without it, bookings add no labour demand and the plan says so.

rows.title: Register a process path
rows.story: An operator seeds a process path with its steps, such as pick then pack. This context keeps its own paths and does not follow the process-path catalogue.

rows.title: Register a capacity limit by hand
rows.story: A planner records one limit on a process at a location for a time window: labour, location, equipment, station, conveyor, buffer or replenishment. The lowest limit is what the process can really do. An announcement goes out only if that figure moves.

rows.title: Draft a capacity plan
rows.story: A planner asks whether a path can handle the demand at a site in a time window. If no demand figure is typed in, the expected orders are used. Dock bookings are priced in labour minutes beside it and never added to order demand.

then.does: keeps the plan's window as a draft in its planned-capacity copy

rows.title: Publish a plan and announce any shortage
rows.story: Publishing makes a draft plan official, once only. If the path can do less than the demand, the shortage and the slowest step are announced too.

then.does: marks the window published and flags orders whose promise falls in a shortage; moves no promise
keeps the published plan window in a local copy; plans without a site are skipped

rows.title: Turn committed shifts into labour limits
rows.story: Each line of a committed shift plan says how many people work a path, at what rate, for how many hours. That becomes a labour limit from the shift start for those hours. The rate is assumed to be units per hour.
rows.policy: Whenever a shift plan line is committed, register its heads times rate as a labour limit for its hours

rows.title: Count a new slot on the floor
rows.story: facility-layout announces each slot. Storage slots add storage positions and work-center slots add stations, per zone. Station counts are multiplied by the declared station standard when a path's capacity is worked out.
rows.policy: Whenever a slot is registered, add it to its zone's count of storage positions or stations

rows.title: Remove a retired slot from the count
rows.story: When facility-layout takes a slot out of service, it comes out of its zone's count. The count only ever follows the floor map and registers no capacity limit itself.
rows.policy: Whenever a slot is decommissioned, take it off its zone's count of positions or stations

rows.title: Keep the expected-orders list
rows.story: Each allocated order, fully or partly, counts once at its latest promise cutoff toward the demand of the configured site. Cancellations are not seen, so the figure can overstate demand.
rows.policy: Whenever an order is allocated, fully or partly, record it at its promise cutoff for the configured site

rows.title: Keep the dock-bookings list
rows.story: dock-scheduling announces bookings, moves, cancellations and no-shows. Each has a version and the newest wins, so a cancellation that arrives first still sticks. Cancelled and missed bookings stop counting as demand.
rows.policy: Whenever a dock appointment is booked, moved, cancelled or missed, update the dock-booking demand copy

rows.title: Count what the floor really completes
rows.story: Completed tasks are counted per process step and minute. A plan's variance view sets them against the planned capacity. It is advice only and never changes a plan.
rows.policy: Whenever a task is completed, add it to the count for its process step and minute

rows.title: Feed the plan reports
rows.story: The service reads its own plan announcements and keeps daily facts for the reports: bottleneck frequency, shortage trend and plan throughput. Capacity-limit events are not part of these reports.
rows.policy: Whenever a plan is created or published, add it to the plan facts behind the reports

hotspots.text: A shift event carries no window or rate unit. The window is the event time plus planned hours, and the unit is assumed to be units per hour.
Order and task events carry no site, so all demand and completions go to one configured site. Cancellations are not netted, so demand can be overstated.
Stations counted without a declared station standard only raise a warning. No throughput is invented for them.
Process paths are seeded by hand. The process-path catalogue is deliberately not consumed.
ProcessCapacityRegistered and ProcessCapacityChanged are published, but their consumer is marked as not built yet.

opportunities.text: Adjusting planned capacity automatically from observed throughput is left to a later decision, which must show it cannot oscillate.
If order events one day carry a usable site, demand can be attributed per site instead of to one configured site.

wes-work-planning.oneLine: Turns a shift's forecast volume into a plan, then releases work to the floor continuously, earliest cut-off first. It watches backlog and flags where to rebalance.

rows.title: Record the volume due by each cut-off
rows.story: A planner records how many units are due by each carrier cut-off for a path. For case picks, the cases, cube and weight are worked out from the SKU's pack facts.

rows.title: Commit the plan for a path
rows.story: A planner commits rate, heads and hours for a path. Heads cannot exceed the stations installed. If workforce-management has already committed a different headcount, the difference is flagged in the same step.

rows.title: Compare with the labour plan
rows.story: workforce-management commits its own headcount per path. This service keeps a read-only copy and, if its own plan for the path has different heads, flags the difference. It only flags; neither plan is corrected.
rows.policy: Whenever the labour plan arrives, keep a copy and flag a difference in heads from our plan

rows.title: Turn an allocated order into work
rows.story: When an order is allocated, fully or in part, each released line becomes one work unit on its process path. A path the catalogue does not know is refused loudly instead of filling a pool nobody serves.
rows.policy: Whenever an order is allocated, enqueue one work unit per released line

then.does: confirms the order line was released to the floor planner, so it knows nothing was lost

rows.title: Turn a stock transfer into work
rows.story: network-inventory-planning releases a transfer demand. It becomes one work unit named after the demand, so a repeat of the same demand never makes a second one. Only transfer legs are accepted, never relocation.
rows.policy: Whenever a transfer demand is released, enqueue one work unit for it

rows.title: Turn an approved slot plan into relocation work
rows.story: slotting-optimization approves a plan of moves. Each move becomes a relocation unit, and a move waiting on another stays blocked until that one completes. A newer plan cancels the older plan's unreleased moves.
rows.policy: Whenever a slot plan is approved, plan one relocation unit per move and cancel older unreleased moves

rows.title: Turn a pick-face top-up request into work
rows.story: pick-face-replenishment asks for a top-up, and it becomes one work unit, urgent ones sorting ahead. A cancellation before release withdraws the unit. Work already released runs to completion.
rows.policy: Whenever a top-up is requested, plan one work unit for it, with a deadline set by its priority

rows.title: Release the next work
rows.story: A supervisor, or an agent, releases the pending work unit with the earliest cut-off. A path fed by release stops at its work-in-progress limit. The release carries hazard hints from the product's classification.

then.does: turns the released work into a floor task needing the skills its path requires

rows.title: Finish a work unit when its task is done
rows.story: When the floor completes the task, the work unit is completed and its slot in the pool is freed. A completed relocation admits the moves that were waiting behind it. Tasks this service never planned are ignored.
rows.policy: Whenever a floor task completes, complete its work unit and free its work-in-progress slot

rows.title: Watch a path's backlog
rows.story: A supervisor samples a path's backlog. Over its alarm threshold, an alarm goes out. If a cut-off time is given, the path's remaining room for new work before it is announced too.

then.does: opens or updates an exception for the path on a backlog alarm
keeps the remaining room per path and cut-off for its delivery promises
keeps the remaining room per path for its own capacity figures

rows.title: Decide how to rebalance a path
rows.story: A supervisor asks what to do about a path. A flow-fed path over its alarm gets 'throttle upstream'. A release-fed path stuck at its limit with work waiting gets 'reassign labour'. Both are flags only. A rate deviation notice is declared but never raised.

rows.title: Set how a path's pool is fed
rows.story: A supervisor sets whether a path is fed by release or by flow, and its work-in-progress limit. Lowering the limit never evicts work: releases just pause until the count falls under it. Nothing is announced.

rows.title: Keep the process-path list
rows.story: process-path-management announces every path defined, revised or retired. When the catalogue source is set to that feed, this service follows it live. By default it reads a file instead.
rows.policy: Whenever a path is created, revised or retired, update the local process-path list

rows.title: Keep the product hazard and pack facts
rows.story: product-master announces each product's classification, such as hazmat or fragile, and its pack levels. This service keeps its own copies and stamps the hints on released work. A newer version replaces an older one.
rows.policy: Whenever a product is classified or its pack level changes, replace the local copy with the newer version

rows.title: Keep the usable-stock view
rows.story: inventory-storage announces stock reserved and reservations revoked. This service keeps a read-only count of usable stock per SKU that operators can look up. No release decision depends on it.
rows.policy: Whenever stock is reserved or a reservation is revoked, adjust the usable-stock count for that SKU

rows.title: Feed the throughput report
rows.story: The service reads its own announcements and keeps hourly figures per path: work released and completed, backlog alarms and throttling. They feed the release throughput report.
rows.policy: Whenever work is released or completed, or an alarm is raised, add it to that path's hourly figures

hotspots.text: RateDeviationDetected is declared but no rule raises it. A test fails if code starts raising it before a decision defines when.
PathPlanDriftDetected has no reader yet. Any reaction by another context, such as an alert, is explicitly deferred.
Remaining room for flow-fed paths is permanently unknown, and a consumer must match it to a cut-off by nearest time because there is no stronger key.
Committing a plan can ask facility-layout live for a travel distance. It is optional and fails open. Moving it to events is a tracked follow-up.

opportunities.text: A real-time, sub-hour observed-throughput figure per flow-fed path is deferred until a consumer needs fresher data than the report.
A cancellation event for unreleased work units can be added if a consumer needs one. Today a cancelled unit is visible only through the read API.
Drift detection could also compare rate and hours, and track drift across shifts. Today it compares planned heads only.

workforce-management.oneLine: Tracks who is on shift and on which process path: commits each shift's headcount plan, assigns certified people to paths and flags paths that are short of people.

rows.title: Propose heads for a path
rows.story: A shift lead asks how many people a path needs for a forecast workload. With no planned rate, the measured rate is used. If people on that work are often idle, the answer is trimmed. Nothing is saved.
rows.policy: Whenever no rate is given, use the measured rate; trim the heads when the idle share is high

rows.title: Commit the shift's headcount split
rows.story: A shift lead commits how many people go on each path. A line is refused if its heads exceed the stations installed, the hours the heads can work or the live station count. One announcement goes out per path line.

then.does: turns each plan line into a labour limit for the shift's hours
keeps the latest labour plan per path and checks it against its own plan

rows.title: Start an associate's shift
rows.story: A shift lead puts an associate on the roster with their certifications and, optionally, their site. Starting again for the same associate restarts the roster entry instead of failing.

rows.title: Certify an associate
rows.story: A shift lead adds a certification, such as pick, pack or hazmat, to an associate on shift. A path that needs a certification can only take people who hold it.

rows.title: Start a break
rows.story: A shift lead logs the start of an associate's break. Nobody can be assigned to a path while on a break.

rows.title: End a break
rows.story: A shift lead logs the end of the break, and the associate can be assigned to a path again.

rows.title: Assign an associate to a path
rows.story: A shift lead, or an agent acting for one, puts an associate on a path. They must hold the path's certification and not be on break. Moving someone ends their old assignment, so nobody is on two paths at once.

rows.title: Spot a path that is short of people
rows.story: Asking for a path's staffing gap compares planned heads with people actually assigned. If the path is short, a notice is raised as a flag only. Nobody is moved: a human decides.

rows.title: End an associate's shift
rows.story: A shift lead ends the shift. The associate's active assignment is closed first and its hours are logged against the shift.
rows.policy: Whenever a shift ends, close the associate's active assignment and log its hours

rows.title: Keep the process-path list
rows.story: process-path-management announces every path that is defined, revised or retired. This context keeps its own list, used to check plans and to work out which certification a path needs.
rows.policy: Whenever a path is created, revised or retired, update the local process-path list

rows.title: Keep the measured rates
rows.story: labor-performance reports how long tasks really take and how idle people are. This context keeps the latest figures per task type, so a proposal can use a real rate and the staffing gap can show idle time.
rows.policy: Whenever a task's performance is recorded, update the measured rate and idle share of its task type

rows.title: Feed the labour report
rows.story: The service reads its own announcements and keeps daily labour figures: shifts, breaks, certifications, assignments and understaffing. They feed the labour report.
rows.policy: Whenever a labour or shift event is announced, add it to that day's labour figures

hotspots.text: Committing a shift plan asks fulfillment-execution live for station counts. If that call fails, the whole commit is refused. Moving it to events is a follow-up.
The installed-station count on a commit is supplied by the caller and cannot be verified here, so a second check against the live count was added.
With no planned rate and no measured rate yet for a path, a proposal comes back with zero heads rather than an error.
Messages that cannot be processed go to a holding area with no alerting and no replay tool.

opportunities.text: The live call to fulfillment-execution for station counts, and the REST rollback for measured rates, are tracked as follow-ups to move onto events.
The deprecated buildingId name will be removed only by a later announced breaking decision; siteCode is already the canonical name.

yard-management.oneLine: The physical yard outside the walls: who passed the gate, where each trailer is, who moves it, and what is done at the door.

rows.title: Check a truck in at the gate
rows.story: The gate clerk records a visit and its trailers. The seal is compared with the booking, and each trailer gets a move: to its door if on time and the door is free, otherwise to a spot. Site policy can turn a seal mismatch or a suspended carrier away.
reads: Yard spots and doors (copy from facility-layout)

then.does: marks the appointment as arrived: early, on time or late
stores the gate arrival, the start of the dock-to-stock clock
opens a case when the seal does not match

rows.title: Turn a truck away at the gate
rows.story: The gate clerk refuses a visit and records the reason. The refused visit is recorded as rejected and gets no trailer.

then.does: cancels the booked appointment with the reason 'turned away'
opens a case for the rejected visit

rows.title: Ask for a trailer to be moved
rows.story: A yard supervisor asks for a trailer to go to a spot or a door. The destination is checked and reserved. The yard also asks by itself: it calls the next trailer in when a door frees up and clears a dropped trailer after door work.
reads: Yard spots and doors (copy from facility-layout)

rows.title: Hand the next move to a yard-truck driver
rows.story: A hostler (yard-truck driver) asks for work. The yard picks the most urgent waiting move and lends it for a limited time. The trailer leaves its place at once; leaving a door frees that door.

then.does: completes the appointment when its trailer leaves the door

rows.title: Park or dock the trailer
rows.story: The hostler reports where the trailer was left. The move ends and the trailer is parked on a spot or docked at a door, in one step. An occupied place is refused and the move stays open.
reads: Yard spots and doors (copy from facility-layout)

then.does: moves the booking to the door the trailer really took, if different
attaches the trailer to the load at that door and starts loading

rows.title: Start work at the door
rows.story: A dock operator starts unloading or loading a docked trailer. If the site asks for it, an unsecured trailer is refused, and so is loading before a required inspection has passed.

rows.title: Secure a docked trailer
rows.story: A dock operator records that the trailer is held to the dock by a vehicle restraint or wheel chocks. It must be docked and have no open move.

rows.title: Finish unloading when the receipt closes
rows.story: inbound-receiving closes a receipt. When every ASN on a docked trailer has a closed receipt, its door work is completed and the trailer counts as empty. Staff can also complete door work by hand.
rows.policy: Whenever the last receipt of a docked trailer closes, complete its door work

then.does: keeps the door-work completion for its load adherence view

rows.title: Release the securing before the trailer leaves
rows.story: A dock operator frees the trailer from restraint or chocks. This is needed before it can leave its door, and is refused while door work is in progress.

rows.title: Inspect a trailer
rows.story: An inspector works through a checklist and completes it. If a required item fails, the inspection fails and the trailer is put on hold in the same step.

rows.title: Release a hold on a trailer
rows.story: A yard supervisor lifts the hold on a trailer, whether it was placed by hand, by a broken seal or by a failed inspection.

rows.title: Check a truck out of the yard
rows.story: The gate clerk lets the visit leave with the trailers it takes. Each must be on site and released, and an inspection before departure may be required. A trailer left behind is a drop and stays.

then.does: confirms the shipment and issues the bill of lading when the load is closed
completes the appointment when its trailer leaves the door

rows.title: Free the yard when a booking falls through
rows.story: dock-scheduling reports a booking cancelled, missed or moved to another door. The yard cancels the open moves that were bringing a trailer to that door. A trailer already on site stays where it is.
rows.policy: Whenever a booking is cancelled, missed or moved, cancel its open hostler moves to the door

rows.title: Take back moves whose lease ran out
rows.story: A sweep looks for claimed moves whose time ran out. Each goes back to the waiting list and its trailer back to where it was, unless that place was taken meanwhile.
rows.policy: Every sweep, put each claimed move whose lease has expired back on the waiting list

rows.title: Chase trailers that stay too long
rows.story: A sweep finds trailers on site whose time reached the limit for their kind and raises one alert for each.
rows.policy: Every sweep, raise a dwell alert once for each trailer past its limit

then.does: opens a case for the overdue trailer

rows.title: Audit the yard against the records
rows.story: A supervisor walks the yard, notes what is at each place, then closes the check. It reports every difference from what the yard believes. A place not seen is missing if a trailer should be there.

then.does: opens one case per difference; a clean check opens none

hotspots.text: A door closure or a retired slot under a trailer already there is not handled. Closures only guard arrival. Handling the case is left to a later phase.
Hazmat and reefer rules trust the declared load. The yard cannot check what a trailer holds, and one classified after parking stays where it is.
Securing, release and inspection results are published but nobody reads them yet.
The event contract does not yet declare who made a change when an agent writes through the tool interface. The data is on the wire.

opportunities.text: exception-management is the planned reader of failed inspections, so that a failure becomes an exception case to work.
A hazmat segregation rule, so classes may not stand on adjacent spots, needs spot neighbours that facility-layout does not publish yet. A later ADR is planned.
